The model also answers with its own transcript, which helps on text-rich images. SEE needs no detector or OCR engine. Across five backbones, SEE improves every small-object benchmark by 2.3-13.1 points and outperforms five training-free baselines on small objects. With SEE, Qwen3.5-4B surpasses the direct answer of Qwen3.5-9B and matches the 6 times larger Qwen3.5-27B.

papers.title: 3DTouch: A Tactile-aware VLA Model with 3D Geometric Relations for Dexterous Manipulation
papers.abstract: In contact-rich dexterous manipulation, occlusion by the fingers and interacting objects obscures local geometry, preventing visual observations from fully capturing contact locations. Visually similar scenes may also differ subtly in the relative positions of interacting objects, leading to different contact states. We propose 3DTouch, a tactile-geometric conditioning approach for vision-language-action (VLA) models. 3DTouch constructs a shared 3D visuo-tactile representation by expressing RGB-D scene points and dense five-finger tactile measurements in the robot-base frame, preserving each taxel's spatial location and force vector. Hand-object and object-object relations derived from hand landmarks and pose-aligned reconstructed surfaces explicitly describe the relative arrangement of interacting entities. Together, these representations condition the VLA action expert on spatially localized contact forces and relative surface geometry, providing explicit cues for contact adjustment and object alignment. We evaluate 3DTouch on five real-world contact-rich dexterous manipulation tasks using a UR7e robot arm equipped with an XHand dexterous hand. 3DTouch improves the average success rate by 42 percentage points over the corresponding VLA baseline and by 20 percentage points over the strongest evaluated alternative. Ablation studies reveal the complementary benefits of scene geometry and spatial tactile feedback, with further gains from shared spatial grounding and explicit geometric relations.

papers.title: Blanket theory for dense networks
papers.abstract: We show how Blanket theory provides a constructive method for calculating cavity functionals in dense spin networks. Building on the description through interfaces and magnetization shells, we develop the calculation from the low-temperature fluctuations around the ground state. In this regime, dilute defects reveal the mechanism of random energy model (REM) universality for linear energies, while their sharing and renewal across layers organize the energies and Gibbs weights into a hierarchy. Because the same configurations determine the covariances of the fresh cavity fields, this construction identifies the fields and weights with an Aizenman-Sims-Starr random overlap structure. The cavity contributions can then be evaluated through recursive fractional means, yielding an explicit free-energy functional parametrized by layer magnetizations and hierarchical exponents, with coefficients determined by the interaction variances and the network normalization. Under the stated moment and normalization conditions, comparison of pressures transfers the limiting mean pressure from the Gaussian representative to networks with independent centered non-Gaussian couplings having the same variances. We illustrate the method with the deterministic Curie-Weiss model, recover the Parisi functional for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, and derive the functionals for restricted and deep Boltzmann machines, including the full replica symmetry breaking (fullRSB) limit.

papers.title: Scattering features of a self-dual spectral singularity in coupled ring resonators with balanced gain and loss
papers.abstract: We theoretically and numerically discuss the general scattering property of a coupled two-ring-resonators externally coupled to a straight bus waveguide. Specifically, we require one ring resonator to be light field amplifying and another to be that dissipative, where the associated attenuation and gain factors for a field amplitude after one-round trip are formed in a reciprocal pair as well as the effective wave propagation constants are same. Obtained from reciprocity and an effective PT-symmetric transfer matrix, we exploit parametrization to propose a general phase diagram, identifying overall scattering outcomes. Especially, we find that the formation of a self-dual spectral singularity, namely coherent perfect absorption-lasing (CPAL), is occurred at a certain relation of a coupling coefficient and an attenuation factor as well as resonant whispering gallery modes. Reducing light amplification and dissipation strengths in each rings narrows the spectral bandwidth associated with CPAL. We further discover that any system with the CPAL parameters would exhibit a same scattering feature: transmission extinction, CPAL, and uni-directional reflectionless at the loss ring side, with respect to an incident wavelength. Additionally, a transmission extinction can be away from the resonance. These analytical predictions are verified by electromagnetic simulations.

papers.title: DORMS: Image Segmentation via Depth-Ordered Region Merge Trees
papers.abstract: We introduce DORMS (Depth-Ordered Region Merging for Segmentation), a purely algorithmic approach to image segmentation from monocular depth maps, requiring no neural networks or learned parameters in the segmentation process. An off-the-shelf monocular depth estimator provides the input depth maps. Our method constructs depth-ordered merge trees through a deterministic union-find sweep, combining component area, depth persistence, and spatial contact constraints to guide region merging. A threshold search determines the segmentation granularity according to a specified target region count, while global depth detrending improves the separation of local geometric structures. Extensive experiments on COCO Panoptic, Cityscapes, and ADE20K demonstrate consistent improvements over classical segmentation baselines and competitive performance against zero-shot neural segmentation models. Notably, our method outperforms all evaluated zero-shot models on Cityscapes, while remaining competitive with several approaches on COCO and ADE20K. These results highlight the potential of purely algorithmic geometric reasoning for image segmentation without learned segmentation models.

papers.title: Spectrum of the parity operator for parafermions and parabosons from character formulas
papers.abstract: In a recent paper [J. Phys. A: Math. Theor. 59 175201 (2026)] Green's triple relations for parafermions and parabosons were extended by including a new operator $P$, referred to as the parity operator. The spectrum of $P$ in Fock space representations was computed, making use of the action of parafermion (resp.\ paraboson) creation and annihilation operators. In the current paper, we adopt a different method to compute the spectrum of $P$, namely using character formulas. For a set of $n$ parafermions, the action of $P$ is deduced from character formulas of $so(2n+2)$. For a set of $n$ parabosons, the known spectrum of $P$ yields new character formulas of particular $osp(2|2n)$ representations.

papers.title: Faster than square-root run-time in adiabatic quantum algorithms for Exact Cover 3
papers.abstract: By intertwining ideas from sequential and adiabatic quantum computing, we propose a quantum algorithm for the problem class Exact Cover 3, which is a sub-class of 3-satisfiability (3-SAT) problems and NP (nondeterministic polynomial time) complete. We find a quantum run-time which is significantly faster than the square-root run-time $N\to N^{1/2}$ of the Grover algorithm. Depending on the structure of the problem (e.g., connectivity of clauses), the run-time scaling may range from approximately third root $N\to N^{1/3}$ to nearly fourth root $N\to N^{1/4}$, possibly even faster.

papers.title: Constraining Accretion Heating in Neutron Stars with Carbon Instability and Quiescent Cooling
papers.abstract: In accreting neutron stars, different heating depths can produce similar quiescent cooling when the heating strength and core temperature are adjusted. For KS 1731-260, we compare thermal histories with accretion heating either in a shallower region that overlaps the carbon fuel layer or in a deeper region below it. Without the carbon instability condition, the two histories fit ten quiescent Chandra spectra nearly equally well. When local carbon instability is required at the observed superburst epoch, the deeper region needs stronger accretion heating than the shallower region. After the thermal and spectral parameters are refitted, the deeper history retains more heat beneath the fuel and produces excess early quiescent emission. A larger fitted absorbing column partly attenuates this excess but makes the late spectra too faint. The fuel temperatures at the superburst epoch are similar in the two histories, so the same prescribed energy release produces nearly identical superburst decays. Including carbon burial, consumption and nuclear heating reduces the accretion heating needed for rapid burning to begin near the observed superburst; shallower heating still fits the quiescent spectra better. This preference persists across the tested fuel depths, fusion rates, distances and absorption treatments. In synthetic examples, carbon in older material allows deeper heating to match the cooling of a shallower-heating reference. Inferring the heating location therefore requires a fuel distribution and thermal history consistent with ignition, burst emission and quiescent cooling.

papers.title: SimplePro: A Simple Baseline for Proactive Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Proactive video understanding requires vision-language models (VLMs) to decide not only what to answer as a video unfolds, but also when newly arrived evidence warrants a response and when to remain silent. Although modern VLMs excel at offline long-video understanding, they struggle in proactive streaming settings, leading prior work to introduce task-specific reinforcement learning or auxiliary triggering modules. We find that explicit reporting rules and structured streaming context substantially improve a frozen VLM's proactive response performance. We exploit this observation to build SIMPLEPRO, a training-free baseline for proactive video understanding. At each decision step, the model combines recent high-resolution frames, bounded historical observations, and prior answer records to determine whether new information warrants a response and, when needed, generate a concise answer. The system then filters consecutive duplicate answers while retaining the raw outputs as context for subsequent decisions. Without any parameter updates or auxiliary triggers, SIMPLEPRO with a 4B backbone consistently outperforms specialized proactive systems across OVO-Bench, StreamingBench-PO, and ProactiveVideoQA. SIMPLEPRO shows overall performance gains as backbone size increases from 2B to 32B. We hope this simple yet effective method will serve as a strong baseline for proactive video understanding, and we will release our code and inference pipeline to support future research.

papers.title: MitoWorld: A Stochastic World Model of the Single-Cell Cycle under Genetic Perturbation
papers.abstract: A cell observed after a gene knockdown has an uncertain future, both in how its appearance will evolve and when it will divide. Existing approaches predict endpoints or population-level changes without jointly modeling individual trajectories and division timing. In this work, we present MitoWorld, a stochastic world model that generates these future appearances as continuous evolution in a Gaussian reference latent, terminated by a division hazard and converted into images by a conditional diffusion renderer. The ordinary transition provably preserves its Gaussian reference, tying its noise to its dynamics; paired observations identify its discrete transition where stationary marginals cannot. The hazard turns division timing into a survival likelihood that can be tested against real cycle lengths. On 325 held-out MitoCheck tracks spanning 17 knockdowns and a control, MitoWorld lowers FID by 34.6\% and the video metric JEDi by 45.6\% relative to the strongest baselines. Its latent-space prediction intervals achieve near-nominal 90\% coverage, are 35\% narrower than those of a model with freely fitted noise. The hazard also yields cell-cycle length distributions with KS distance close to the model-based finite-sample reference. Testable single-cell stochastic dynamics thus offer a generative tool for time-lapse perturbation screens.

papers.title: Exploiting Common Volatility Dynamics in High-Dimensional Portfolio Selection
papers.abstract: We study how commonalities in monthly realized stock volatilities can be exploited for high-dimensional covariance forecasting and portfolio selection. We compare latent factor models with ARMA models that pool dynamic parameters within pre-specified groups of stocks. We show that pooled ARMA models admit an exact dynamic factor representation with group-specific dynamics and stock-specific loadings. The implied static factor representation involves group-specific factors that need not be pervasive. Combining volatility forecasts with realized dynamic conditional correlations and nonlinear shrinkage, we evaluate out-of-sample minimum variance portfolios of S&P 500 constituents. Pooling-based approaches consistently outperform the alternatives across portfolio constraints and model specifications.

papers.title: WAIVES: Weak-form Asymptotically-unbiased Instrumental-Variable Estimation for SDEs
papers.abstract: Weak-form methods have transformed inference for deterministic dynamical systems. By integrating the governing equations against smooth, compactly supported test functions, they trade noise-amplifying differentiation for noise-attenuating integration, yielding fast and robust estimates. Extending this idea to stochastic differential equations (SDEs) has proven harder, and a consistent single-trajectory formulation has remained out of reach. Applied naively in the time domain, the weak form makes the regressors and the errors functionals of the same noise, creating endogeneity that leaves weak-form least squares biased and inconsistent. We resolve it with instrumental variables, a classical idea from econometrics. Weak-form integrals over nearby disjoint time windows prove to be valid instruments, correlated with the regressors yet uncorrelated with the error, restoring consistency and asymptotic normality. The resulting generalized-method-of-moments estimator, WAIVES (Weak-form Asymptotically-unbiased Instrumental-Variable Estimation for SDEs), requires only a linear solve, with no likelihood evaluations, filtering, or simulation. It is therefore an order of magnitude faster than exact-likelihood methods where those exist, and it applies unchanged where they do not, with standard errors and calibrated confidence intervals supplied by the moment conditions. It also separates measurement noise from the intrinsic randomness of the dynamics. Across nine example systems, spanning linear, bistable, chaotic, excitable, state-dependent-diffusion, non-polynomial, hypoelliptic, and high-dimensional regimes (up to 120 dimensions), WAIVES recovers nonlinear drift and diffusion with negligible bias and near-nominal interval coverage. We close with two real-data illustrations: a 167-year North Atlantic sea-surface-temperature record and an optical-tweezer calibration.

papers.title: VOL-Agent: Programming Your Film via Video Orchestration Language Agentic System
papers.abstract: Recent video foundation models generate high-quality and limited-length clips, but orchestrating them into minute-level, story-coherent films remains an open problem. Existing video agents highly rely on natural-language planning or predefined workflows, which make their production hard to program, customize, and extend. Therefore, we introduce VOL-Agent, a programmable video agent built on a Video Orchestration Language (VOL). With static compilation and verification, followed by runtime dynamic loading, VOL-Agent decouples structural reliability from execution flexibility. Through the skill-driven executor, VOL-Agent dynamically resolves tools and skills from an open-world repository and supports user-defined skills in natural language. Moreover, VOL-Agent is capable of crafting new director skills from learned knowledge and improves itself through feedback to accumulate filmmaking knowledge. To overcome the disconnect between different segments, we apply a structural memory mechanism to record and recall world and entity states, sustaining entity and scene consistency across different shots. Critic feedback supports local revision, while reusable filmmaking knowledge and experiences can be retained for subsequent tasks. Experiments on three benchmarks show that VOL-Agent generates minute-scale videos with strong overall quality and limited cost.

papers.title: Incremental Speciation in Evolutionary Red Teaming of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Speciation maintains distinct subpopulations in evolutionary search through similarity-based grouping and species-aware parent selection. For text-based individuals, niches depend on both the compatibility representation and the assignment operator that turns pairwise relations into species. We examine this design space in black-box evolutionary red teaming of large language models, comparing embedding and natural language inference (NLI) dissimilarities under representative-based and density-based speciation. Offline calibration on a 3,139-prompt archive shows that MiniLM embedding dissimilarity ($d_E$) and DeBERTa-v3-small NLI non-entailment ($d_{\neg E}$) produce different species structures at the same nominal threshold. Even with pairwise edge density matched to MiniLM, NLI density connectivity forms a few concentrated, mixed-topic species, with substantially more off-topic membership. These structural differences persist online under a matched evaluation budget. The endpoint top-50 median fitness favors incremental DBSCAN over leader-follower, but bootstrap intervals from 10 runs include zero, providing no reliable evidence of an advantage. Semantic diversity among top prompts declines in every configuration, with no consistent method advantage. The clearest difference concerns high-fitness population occupancy: MiniLM incremental DBSCAN maintains mature niches across seed topics, whereas NLI incremental DBSCAN attains the same highest observed median fitness while concentrating high-fitness prompts in variants of a few seed topics. Thus, representation-dependent connectivity predicts population structure more consistently than endpoint fitness. Species count alone does not establish quality-diversity, and more species do not necessarily preserve semantically diverse high-fitness prompts.

papers.title: Projection-Based and Modulus-Based Equivalent Reformulations of the Linear Complementarity Problem and Corresponding Iterative Methods: A Review
papers.abstract: The Linear Complementarity Problem (LCP) is a fundamental mathematical model arising in optimization, equilibrium theory, and various scientific and engineering applications. Its complementarity structure admits several equivalent mathematical representations, which provide a foundation for developing a wide range of iterative solution methods. This review presents a systematic and critical analysis of the principal reformulations of the LCP, with particular emphasis on minimum-function, projection-based, positive-negative part, and modulus-based formulations. The mathematical equivalence of these representations to the standard LCP is examined, highlighting their underlying relationships and the preservation of the complementarity conditions. Building upon these formulations, the review surveys the corresponding iterative methods developed in the existing literature, focusing on their mathematical foundations, algorithmic structures, and convergence requirements. A comparative perspective is developed to discuss the relative advantages and limitations of the different approaches, emphasizing that the suitability of an iterative method depends on the structural properties of the underlying LCP and the specific algorithm employed. In addition, relevant performance measures, including iteration count, CPU time, complementarity residual, memory requirements, and parameter sensitivity, are discussed as criteria for numerical evaluation. Finally, the review identifies important challenges and potential research directions, particularly in adaptive parameter selection, effective matrix-splitting strategies, scalable implementations, and reproducible numerical benchmarking, with the aim of supporting the development of reliable and computationally efficient methods for solving LCPs

papers.title: When Do Decision Models Help LLM-Driven Network Discovery?
papers.abstract: Network discovery, the identification of live hosts and their exposed services, is the first phase of every penetration test, and it is increasingly automated by harnesses driven by large language models (LLMs). To mitigate hallucinated or unsafe commands, recent work proposes inserting fast, non-generative decision models to validate actions prior to execution. This paper quantifies whether such validation improves discovery across three network scales (n = 10, 100, and 1,000) in a simulation calibrated on a 30-node containerized testbed. Our findings show that chunked batch dispatch recovers 92% to 100% of open ports in large-scale networks, whereas single-host dispatch collapses to under 6% due to context saturation and scan latency. Furthermore, at the measured proposal quality of the local model, decision gating increases its port recall from 75.5% to 89.0% on small networks and intercepts costly decoy tarpits, but it imposes additional latency on frontier models during early host discovery.

papers.title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?
papers.abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents are widely trained in executable GUI environments. To lower cost, build environments in batches, and reduce manual effort, each work trades away part of the environment through its construction choices. We describe these choices along three dimensions: reward coverage, the goal-reaching trajectories the verifier rewards; data coverage, the application data the agent is exposed to beyond what the task reads or writes; and feature coverage, the application features beyond what the task uses. Existing works set each dimension on engineering grounds, but they do not measure its effect on training. How complete must an environment be to train a capable agent, and along which dimensions? In MobileGym, we adjust each dimension separately, train Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, and evaluate every policy in the original full environment. A verifier that rewards only one reference path lowers success by 10.53 points, and removing unneeded records also lowers success. Pruning unneeded features instead raises success from 51.61% to 56.13%, entirely on tasks whose environments it left unchanged. The gain reverses when each episode is weighted equally and vanishes when only episodes on the pruned tasks are balanced. Without pruning, length weighting there reinforces long detour successes that erode skills on other tasks. Following these findings, we build MobileGym-Lite, which keeps reward and data coverage complete and prunes unneeded features. It outperforms Full in the full environment (55.48% versus 51.61% success) with lower construction cost.

papers.title: The algebraic classification of three-dimensional nilpotent left-symmetric dialgebras
papers.abstract: Left-symmetric dialgebras (LSDA) are to left-symmetric algebras what Leibniz algebras are to Lie algebras. We classify the three-dimensional nilpotent LSDA over the complex numbers. To do this we adapt the annihilator-extension (Skjelbred-Sund) method to dialgebras, using the annihilator with respect to both products on both sides, and we compute the second cohomology of all two-dimensional nilpotent LSDA. Up to isomorphism, besides the null and split algebras there are nine non-split algebras and families; the 2-step nilpotent families depend on four and three parameters. We give isomorphism criteria and separating invariants, identify the left-symmetric and diassociative algebras in the list, and complete the two-dimensional classification of an earlier paper.

papers.title: SIGNTOK: A Text-Aligned Continuous Pose Tokenizer for Sign Language Generation
papers.abstract: Text-conditioned sign language generation (SLG) depends not only on the generator but also on the space in which signing is generated. Existing approaches generate directly in pose space, in quantized code spaces, or in learned latent spaces trained for reconstruction. We find that these spaces are organized largely by signer identity rather than linguistic content: on CSL-Daily, a test clip's nearest neighbor in raw pose space is the same sentence signed by another person in only 2% of cases. To address this, we propose SIGNTOK, a continuous pose tokenizer whose latent space is shaped by three training-only heads: a kinematics head that predicts motion dynamics, a sentence-level head that aligns signing with the overall text, and a word-level head that aligns short motion windows with content words. Together, these objectives raise the same-sentence cross-signer nearest-neighbor rate to 82%. On three sign language benchmarks, the same generator trained in the SIGNTOK latent instead of pose space raises back-translation BLEU-4 in five of six benchmark-scorer settings at comparable joint accuracy, and word-level alignment gives higher back-translation scores than sentence-level alignment on every benchmark.

papers.title: Analysis of the Second-Harmonic Generation Process in Nonlinear Metasurfaces Based on Multiple Quantum Wells: The Approach of Nonlinear Current Density, and The Development of Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: Using plasmonic metasurfaces integrated with nonlinear materials, such as multiple quantum wells (MQWs), has been an excellent solution to enhance nonlinear light-matter interactions. In this approach, a plasmonic resonator enhances the intensity of the fundamental harmonic within the MQWs region, increasing the strength of the intersubband transitions inside the MQWs. As a result, the efficiency of second harmonic generation (SHG) increases significantly. In this paper, we present a new approach to analyze the SHG process in nonlinear metasurfaces based on MQWs. In this approach, first, we formulate the nonlinear current density within the MQW region, which serves as the radiation source of the second harmonic wave. Notably, the saturation effect in MQWs, that limits the nonlinear response, is accounted for. Second, we address the development of boundary conditions for the second harmonic (SH) field in periodic structures, which ultimately leads us to define periodic boundary conditions for the SH field. Third, we combine these elements into a semi-analytical framework and validate it against previously reported experimental data. Finally, an efficient MQWs structure and plasmonic metasurface are designed for the fundamental wavelength of 8 $\mu$m. After implementing the proposed algorithm, we observe that the designed nonlinear metasurface achieves a significant conversion efficiency of 0.02% under the incident intensity of 23.5 kW/cm$^2$. KEYWORDS: Second harmonic generation, metasurface, multiple quantum wells, nonlinear current density, periodic boundary conditions

papers.title: GLIDE: Scalable and Event-Aware Inductive Forecasting over Evolving Logistics Graphs
papers.abstract: Accurate forecasting of order volume at scale-effect hotspots (SEHs), spatially coherent groups of logistics flows that serve as distributed optimization units for real-time many-to-one dispatch, is a prerequisite for efficient order pooling in on-demand food delivery (OFD) platforms such as Meituan. However, real-world logistics networks present unique challenges that render standard spatiotemporal prediction model ineffective. (i) Dynamic Topology: Unlike static road networks, logistics graphs are ephemeral, with hotspot emerging and vanishing continuously; (ii) Scale--Volume Heterogeneity: Graph sizes vary from $10^2$ to $10^4$, while zero-inflated, long-tailed volumes create computational bottlenecks and bias predictions toward inactivity; and (iii) Event-Driven Disruption: Exogenous events (holidays, weather, academic calendars) induce systematic demand shifts that purely data-driven backbones cannot anticipate. In this paper, we present GLIDE, a production-ready framework that models evolving logistics graphs in a scalable latent space while adapting to heterogeneous demand regimes and event-driven shifts. GLIDE introduces a Graph-Guided Latent Aggregation mechanism, which dynamically projects varying physical subgraphs into a fixed-size, semantically stable latent space via a differentiable sparse assignment...

papers.title: Angular Conditional Distillation: Overcoming Classifier Geometry Mismatch
papers.abstract: Classifier outputs provide a fundamental and univer- sally available knowledge interface for knowledge distil- lation (KD). However, standard logit objectives entangle transferable semantic relations with architecture-dependent parameterization artifacts, causing a classifier geometry mismatch that makes direct knowledge transfer unreliable. To address this, we propose Angular Conditional Distilla- tion (ACD). First, the Angular Coordinate Interface (ACI) reconstructs the student classifier using angular coordi- nates, suppressing magnitude and bias effects to provide a geometry-compatible space. Then, Scale-Invariant Condi- tional Distillation (SICD) standardizes outputs and exclu- sively transfers conditional non-target relations, filtering out untransferable absolute confidence. Together, ACI de- fines where to transfer, while SICD defines what to transfer. Extensive experiments show that ACD achieves state-of-the- art performance over existing KD methods. Moreover, as a universal drop-in replacement, it consistently improves existing distillation pipelines while requiring no feature adapters or additional inference-time cost. Code is avail- able at https://github.com/laniusnan/ACD.

papers.title: Physical Layer Security for Digital Semantic Communication: A Bit-Level Perspective
papers.abstract: Digital semantic communication requires reliable recovery of task-relevant information at a legitimate receiver while limiting source reconstruction by an eavesdropper. Uniform bit protection, however, does not account for the heterogeneous reliability and secrecy requirements of semantic bits. This paper proposes a bit-level physical layer security (PLS) framework that learns these requirements and incorporates them into physical-layer resource allocation. We first introduce a wiretap semantic feature channel whose two-stage training learns per-bit target bit-flip probabilities for the legitimate receiver (Bob) and the eavesdropper (Eve). These targets characterize the reliability requirements at Bob and the secrecy protection requirements against Eve. Based on the learned targets, we formulate a joint power and artificial-noise (AN) allocation problem for a multiple-input single-output wiretap channel under a worst-case angular-separation model. For a given target profile, the optimal information-AN power split admits a closed-form solution, and the per-bit power allocation is obtained by water-filling. We further develop a leakage-aware selection method among multiple learned-target profiles and extend the design to multiple-input multiple-output channels. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a better trade-off between preserving reconstruction quality at Bob and degrading that at Eve than uniform power allocation and the evaluated learning-based secure semantic communication schemes.

papers.title: Effects of Locomotion and Viewpoint Control on Immersive Robot Telepresence for Navigation and Inspection
papers.abstract: In many robot telepresence interfaces, movement and viewing are managed through handheld inputs. This can divide attention between steering, looking, and inspection. We compared joystick versus omnidirectional treadmill locomotion and joystick-based versus head-guided camera control in a within-subject 2x2 study in which 17 participants used a virtual reality headset to guide a quadruped robot through a physical maze while locating marked wall symbols and capturing them as visual evidence. Mixed-effects analyses showed that head-guided camera control was associated with faster completion, lower wall-contact cost, lower workload, and more favorable presence, usability, technology acceptance, and flow than joystick-based camera control. The strongest overall objective performance was observed in the joystick locomotion plus head-guided camera condition, whereas the omnidirectional treadmill plus head-guided camera condition emerged as the strongest experiential compromise. Exploratory camera analyses showed that head-guided camera control reduced switching, increased reliance on the pan-tilt view, and supported a more stable viewing strategy across the maze. These strategy differences were consistent with the performance advantage, especially for wall-contact duration. Targets captured remained near ceiling and simulator sickness remained low across all conditions. Overall, the results indicate that viewpoint control was the stronger differentiator in this combined navigation and inspection task, while locomotion still shaped the objective and experiential tradeoff.

papers.title: Can you make models believe false facts in the prompt?
papers.abstract: Making LLMs believe false facts is useful for alignment evaluations and for building model organisms. Previous work explored doing so with Synthetic Document Finetuning (SDF). But SDF requires fine-tuning one new model for each set of injected false beliefs. To enable larger scale SDF-powered alignment evaluations, we attempt to produce a single model that believes any fact placed in a tag in the prompt. To do so, we explore doing prompt-conditioned SDF: fine-tuning a model on synthetic documents covering thousands of facts, with each document conditioned on a fact presented in the prompt. We evaluate how deeply the model believes the facts provided in the prompt using evaluations from prior work and a new Jacobian lens evaluation. We find that the belief depth on unseen facts scales roughly log-linearly with the number of training facts, making this a cheap, promising avenue for making models believe false facts, though preliminary experiments on applying it to alignment audits on the small model we studied showed negative results due to these small models often already acting as if they believed facts provided in regular honeypot system prompts. Using RL to reduce the rate at which models verbalize following a false fact in the prompt, on top of prompt-conditioned SDF, generalizes to held-out evals and almost matches SDF on some evaluations. But training against one of our metrics for belief depth makes it harder to trust those evaluations.

papers.title: Stability for the Navier--Stokes and Incompressible Porous Media Equations with Only Vertical Dissipation on $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: For the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^2$, we prove that vertical viscosity alone yields global $H^2$ stability and algebraic decay of the vorticity and velocity for small reflection-symmetric data with polynomially weighted vorticity. Under stronger smallness assumptions, we obtain $H^3$ stability and vorticity-gradient decay, in contrast to unbounded gradient growth for Euler flows in the same symmetry class. For incompressible porous media (IPM), we obtain $H^2$ stability and decay under analogous assumptions with only vertical diffusion, despite the absence of derivative gain in Darcy's law. This complements finite-time blow-up constructions for nondiffusive IPM in periodic domains. The proofs combine a weighted inequality for odd functions with anisotropic energy estimates exploiting the structure of each system.

papers.title: PGU-Decoder: Prior-Guided Unified Decoding for Industrial Road-Network Map Updating
papers.abstract: Timely road-network map updates are essential to navigation and autonomous driving. Three key tasks are intra-intersection road network generation, merging/diverging detection, and drivable-area detection, covering topology, geometry, and attributes, respectively. Separate pipelines duplicate rule maintenance, quality assurance, and manual verification, increasing operational costs. We propose PGU-Decoder, a production-grade unified decoding framework for semantic prediction across these tasks. A Prior Query Module (PQM) constructs point-level prior queries from sampled locations on road-network geometries. Fixed reference points preserve positional priors throughout decoding, allowing the model to focus on surrounding context. Point-level representations are aggregated into instance-level representations, and a Relational Graph Attention Network (RGAT) captures inter-instance dependencies. Task-specific heads then generate predictions. We validate PGU-Decoder in large-scale automated road-network map updating across more than 360 cities in China, where it consistently outperforms seven baselines. Following deployment at AutoNavi Map, it achieves quality scores above 98% on all three tasks, reduces manual verification costs by 95%, and increases update frequency from weekly to hourly. These results demonstrate a practical and cost-effective industrial solution for road-network map updating.

papers.title: Facet-SLAM: Real-Time Triangle Splatting SLAM
papers.abstract: Dense SLAM systems based on 3D Gaussian splatting build maps that render photorealistically, but their surface geometry is poor, and obtaining a mesh requires extraction or fusion stages. Triangle splatting avoids this with surface primitives whose vertices can be triangulated directly into a connected mesh, yet SLAM with this representation has so far relied on photometric tracking, which is too slow for localization at sensor rate. We present Facet-SLAM, the first real-time triangle splatting SLAM system for RGB-D cameras. Fast geometric registration is the natural alternative, but it is not sufficient alone, since the mapper's optimization displaces triangles from the observed surface and makes them unreliable registration targets. We therefore separate the two roles: the tracker sets each triangle's centroid from fused depth and registers frames to these centroids by GICP, while the mapper is restricted to non-translating updates via a change of variables. Our system achieves competitive tracking accuracy at around 100 FPS on a desktop GPU and runs at sensor rate on a Jetson AGX Orin. Compared with the photometric approach, it is over 20 times faster, matches rendering quality, and improves surface accuracy, reducing the chamfer distance of the Delaunay mesh on Replica from 1.55 to 0.86 cm. We will release the implementation at https://github.com/edward62740/Facet-SLAM.

papers.title: What Right-Angle Corners Reveal About an Uncalibrated Camera: Convex Cones, Certified Bounds and Identifiability
papers.abstract: The corner of a box or a room, where three perpendicular edges meet, appears in an image as three segments meeting at a point. We ask what such junctions reveal about an uncalibrated camera's intrinsic parameters. Each junction is consistent with an explicit convex set of cameras; when only the focal length is unknown, this set is an interval in closed form. These sets are computed from the image alone, so calibrating from many junctions is a convex feasibility problem. Almost every junction bounds the focal length from below; we characterize when one also bounds it from above, and when many junctions determine it exactly. For a known vertex, the bounds can be certified against any bounded error in the measured edge directions.

papers.title: TRoPE: Topology-aware Relative Positional Encoding for 4D Generation
papers.abstract: Video-to-4D mesh generation has made substantial progress in recovering dynamic 3D geometry and motion from monocular videos. However, commonly used feed-forward approaches remain prone to sticking artifacts, where geodesically distant vertices move together incorrectly when they become spatially close. We attribute this failure to cross-part motion leakage: spatially nearby yet structurally distant vertices may retrieve similar motion information when motion decoding fails to distinguish spatial proximity from mesh connectivity. To address this issue, we introduce TRoPE, a topology-aware relative positional encoding that makes mesh connectivity explicit in the interaction between vertex queries and mesh-supported motion sources. TRoPE derives spectral features from the graph Laplacian and constructs pairwise topological relations from distances between multi-scale diffusion features, using these relations to modulate vertex--anchor attention through rotary phases. We further introduce a vertex-wise tail-risk objective that emphasizes persistently high-error vertices to explicitly suppress sticking artifacts. To better characterize and quantify these failures, we introduce MeshSticking-4D, a dedicated benchmark for this failure mode. Experiments on MeshSticking-4D show that TRoPE suppresses sticking artifacts while improving overall motion accuracy. Compared with the baseline, it reduces the worst-vertex error by 39.4% and lowers the separation failure rate from 49.35% to 34.90%. Additional evaluations on Motion-80 and Motion324-Subset show lower tail errors on diverse objects, while transfer to Mesh4D demonstrates applicability across backbones.

papers.title: Emo-H2A: Driving a Facial Robot Directly from LLM Hidden States at Token Rate
papers.abstract: Diverse, semantically synchronized, and low-latency facial expressions are essential for human-robot interaction. While large language models (LLMs) have endowed anthropomorphic robots with fluent speech, facial expression still struggles to follow the conversation. Motivated by this gap, we present Emo-H2A (hidden-to-actuation), a paradigm that drives a facial robot directly from LLM hidden states during autoregressive decoding. Without a separate emotion label, expression stays continuous and context-sensitive, and the face moves with the unfolding reply. We instantiate this paradigm as EmoManifold, a training-free method that extracts a valence-arousal-dominance (VAD) coordinate from each hidden state, projects it, and drives the face at token granularity. The readout is checked on six language models, and the same projection drives our 29-degree-of-freedom (DoF) facial robot. When driven by this projection, the face shifts its expression in the matching direction on 87.5% of within-reply valence transitions, whereas holding a single label for the whole reply leaves directional tracking near the 50% chance level, and first moves in 0.96s rather than waiting 10-26s for the reply to finish and a turn-level label to return.

papers.title: Quantifying the Intrusiveness of Retrofitting Retrieval-Augmented Generation onto Legacy Software Systems
papers.abstract: Enterprises increasingly add retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to existing REST and monolithic systems, usually by writing an ad hoc HTTP call into a handler, and have no way to quantify how intrusive that choice is. We present (1) a taxonomy of three retrofit patterns, sidecar, SDK-embed and naive-invasive; (2) the Legacy Intrusion Score (LIS), three code sub-metrics (churn, breadth, coupling), and an extension, LIS-X, with three operational sub-metrics measured on a live system (run-time overhead, fault propagation and silent feature degradation); (3) a static evaluation on five legacy systems, two of them real open-source codebases fetched from their repositories at pinned commits; and (4) a live case study that deploys all three patterns as separate OS processes. The code-level ranking sidecar < SDK-embed < naive-invasive holds in all five systems and under 2,000 random weightings, but it follows from component-wise dominance of the sub-metrics, so it validates the metric rather than testing a hypothesis. In the live study, outcomes are not fixed by definition. The sidecar adds no detectable latency to the legacy endpoint (0.07 ms, 95% CI [-0.10, 0.24]), whereas SDK-embed and naive-invasive add 569 and 475 ms and are not distinguishable from each other (p=0.62). Both pass a 2 s dependency delay on to legacy requests, and when the RAG layer fails fast they keep returning successful responses that no longer contain the AI field. Load on the RAG layer slows the legacy service by 1.51-1.57x on a shared host, and sidecar staleness averages 911 ms with a 2 s polling interval. Retrieval hit@1 is 0.95; three hosted LLMs answer all 12 test questions correctly and a local model 9/12, and the four backends are swapped by changing one request field. All dynamic results come from one host and one system.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Onboard Vision-Language-Navigation Framework for Aerial Robots in Complex Environments
papers.abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are expected to achieve semantic reasoning, intelligent decision-making, and long-horizon navigation under strict onboard constraints. While recent foundation-model-driven approaches have shown promising progress toward this goal, existing methods remain limited by challenges in 3D data availability, trajectory feasibility, long-horizon reasoning, and computational efficiency in complex environments. To bridge these gaps, we propose VLN-AR, a hierarchical vision-language-navigation (VLN) framework for aerial robots. VLN-AR decouples multimodal reasoning and low-level control, enabling structured prediction of 3D pose commands and navigation intentions that are translated into dynamically feasible actions. To mitigate data scarcity and domain gaps, we introduce a fully automated 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-based pipeline to generate scalable photorealistic UAV navigation data. A progressive three-stage training strategy further enhances grounding, scene reasoning, and complex navigation. In addition, a lightweight cognitive agent improves long-horizon reasoning via memory-aware task decomposition. Finally, we design onboard optimization techniques, including token sparsification and model lightweighting, achieving 7.1x-9.4x speedup while maintaining high navigation performance on resource-limited UAV platforms. Experiments show great improvements over existing methods in both simulation and real-world UAV navigation. Project website: https://wyz000.github.io/VLN-AR/

papers.title: ProxySearch: Decoupled Inference-Time Scaling for Diffusion Models via Asymmetric Noise-Rank Transfer
papers.abstract: Noise search at inference time improves text-to-image diffusion but requires many multi-step teacher rollouts per query. Distilled few-step models are now routinely released, yet their potential as proxies inside noise search is uncharacterized. We measure proxy-teacher rank agreement across three distillation regimes and three backbones (DiT, MMDiT, UNet) and find a sharp asymmetry. On our main pool, closed-form image statistics transfer from the proxy to the teacher (Spearman $\rho$ up to 0.80), while learned semantic scorers do not ($\rho \le$ 0.12). Paired null controls trace this rank to the first denoising step for coarse statistics and to distillation for finer ones. We use the asymmetry for noise search under a joint constraint: a semantic reward specifies content, and a numeric target specifies image statistics. In PROXYSEARCH, the proxy filters candidates by statistical match in 1 step, and the teacher returns the survivor with the highest semantic reward. No weight trades one objective against the other. On FLUX-1024, PROXYSEARCH tightens the statistical target by 21-23% at the same number of teacher trajectories, with no detected loss on the optimized reward.

papers.title: Rigidity of randomly perturbed expanding circle maps
papers.abstract: We extend the classical smooth linearization theory of expanding circle maps to randomly perturbed ones without requiring small perturbations, establishing two equivalent rigidity criteria of absolute continuity of random conjugacy and Lyapunov exponents along random periodic orbits. In the random setting, an essential difficulty is the uniqueness of absolutely continuous random invariant measures. For the first criterion, we overcome this difficulty by refining the memory-loss argument of Ott, Stenlund and Young, which gives the exponential convergence of probability densities, to establish the uniqueness of random invariant measures; for the second criterion, we bypass this difficulty by employing periodic-orbital averaging together with Jensen's equality condition to derive pointwise rigidity directly from the periodic data.

papers.title: Trade-off Between Airspace and Channel Capacity for Low-altitude Wireless Network
papers.abstract: Communication-serviceable capacity for low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks depends on both spatial occupancy and wireless quality of service (QoS). This paper formulates a communication-feasible occupancy-planning model that maps candidate-grid assignments to concurrent beam loads and per-user rates under fixed-stream and fixed-beam power. With fixed effective noise, per-beam QoS screening determines maximum admission, and an exact dynamic program maximizes aggregate spectral efficiency at that fixed admission. Signal-level simulations validate the SINR expressions, while an explicit-array model examines load-dependent inter-beam leakage. The dynamic program is globally optimal for the separable integer problem, but that guarantee does not extend to the coupled problem. Equal-time orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and ideal-SIC non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) are evaluated through the same local beam reduction under fixed effective noise and fixed per-beam power.

papers.title: GTI: Grounding Task Intent Throughout Long-Horizon VLA Manipulation
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models generate local actions from visual observations, language, and robot state, but long-horizon manipulation requires the global task intent to remain grounded in the currently executable context. We propose GTI (Grounding Task Intent), which uses the current observation and execution history to localize the active subtask and its execution phase. For the same local subtask, GTI generates two phase-dependent visual targets: an interaction/contact state and a local completion state. The local language instruction and the corresponding phase-specific visual target jointly condition the VLA, specifying both what to do now and what state should be reached at the current phase. During execution, anomaly monitoring and local recovery re-establish an intent-consistent execution context through rollback, re-observation, and phase re-evaluation after persistent deviation. We evaluate GTI on RoboCasa365, VLA-Arena Horizon-Long, and real-world PiPER tasks. Relative to matched Global-FT baselines, GR00T success on seen composite RoboCasa365 tasks increases from 14.6%/12.1% to 31.8%/20.4% under ID/OOD evaluation. On VLA-Arena, GTI+$\pi_{0.5}$ reaches 47.6% overall success versus 45.2% for an adapted ForeAct baseline, with gains of 5.2/6.0 percentage points on the harder L1/L2 tasks. In the three real-robot task experiments, mean full-task success increases from 21.7% to 59.2%. The results indicate that persistent semantic intent localization and phase-conditioned visual grounding improve multi-stage execution, while failure-triggered local recovery provides additional deployment-time support.

papers.title: Cardiac MRI-informed electrocardiography enables biologically grounded cardiomyopathy detection
papers.abstract: Precise myocardial phenotyping at population scale is limited by the cost and accessibility of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), whereas electrocardiography (ECG) is widely available but reflects electrical rather than structural and functional information. Here we develop MyoECG, a cross-modal representation learning framework that distils myocardial structural and functional knowledge from CMR into standard 12-lead ECGs, enabling imaging-informed cardiomyopathy detection and subtype classification from ECGs alone. MyoECG was pretrained on 45,241 paired ECG-CMR examinations from UK Biobank and a tertiary cardiovascular centre, then developed and validated across more than 1.8 million ECGs from seven independent datasets. Across internal and external datasets spanning prevalences of 0.2-54.7%, MyoECG outperformed five pretrained ECG foundation models, with AUROCs of 0.800-0.974 for cardiomyopathy detection. In a multi-reader study of six cardiologists, MyoECG assistance improved mean sensitivity by 0.109 (95% CI, 0.041-0.175; P = 0.009) and specificity by 0.056 (95% CI, 0.004-0.108; P = 0.040). In 41,128 UK Biobank participants, the MyoECG score showed genetic correlations with cardiomyopathy (rg = 0.409) and dilated cardiomyopathy (rg = 0.371), genome-wide associations at four loci, including regions mapped to NFIA and KCNQ1, and associations with 69 circulating proteins related to myocardial stress, cell adhesion, vascular biology and metabolism. The cardiomyopathy correlation attenuated to non-significance after adjustment for 27 measured CMR traits (rg = 0.131; P = 0.143), indicating that the score captures CMR-derived information rather than dataset-specific shortcuts. MyoECG offers a scalable route to CMR-informed cardiomyopathy assessment and a strategy for transferring knowledge from resource-intensive imaging to widely deployable physiological signals.

papers.title: Precision Measurements of the Effective Leptonic Weak Mixing Angle at Hadron Colliders
papers.abstract: We review precision determinations of the effective leptonic weak mixing angle, $\sin^2\theta^\ell_{\mathrm{eff}}$, from Drell-Yan angular asymmetries at the Tevatron and the LHC. As statistical uncertainties have dramatically decreased, parton distribution function (PDF) uncertainty now dominates the most precise hadron-collider results. We describe the angular observables, electroweak calculation schemes, and advanced methods such as replica reweighting and Hessian profiling, used to constrain PDFs directly from measured angular distributions. To identify the origin of differences between modern PDF sets (e.g., CT18, MSHT20, NNPDF) in the extracted mixing angle, we employ a simplified leading-order Z-pole calculation that separates quark-flavor production weights from quark-direction dilution. We demonstrate how these PDF-induced differences can be mitigated by incorporating complementary constraints from W/Z cross-section ratios and W-boson decay asymmetries. Furthermore, we discuss the requirements for a common reinterpretation and future combination of LHC measurements, highlighting how correlated PDF uncertainties limit the ultimate combined precision. Finally, we outline future prospects, including complementary measurements in $Z+b$ production and high-mass tests of the running $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ weak mixing angle.

papers.title: General Noise Channels and Mid-Circuit Measurements for Pre-Trajectory Sampling with Batched Execution
papers.abstract: Many studies of quantum protocols require fast sampling of large amounts of measurement data from noisy quantum circuits, such as for training machine-learning decoders for quantum error correction. Exact simulation of realistic noise is expensive, while stabilizer-based simulators are fast but approximate, for example through Pauli twirling, which generally alters the output statistics. Pre-trajectory sampling with batched execution (PTSBE) accelerates exact trajectory simulation by sampling noise before state evolution. This method requires the outcome probability of every stochastic event to be independent of the state, which excludes mid-circuit measurements and general Kraus channels. We present a generalization of PTSBE to measurement and Kraus operators without approximation. Each event is partially pre-sampled, while deferred outcomes are drawn during grouped execution via multinomial branching and cached-state reuse. We implement the method for GPUs as an extension of CUDA-Q. On distance-3 topological code memories under amplitude damping, it is up to 24x faster than conventional trajectory sampling in CUDA-Q. On 30-qubit random circuits with mid-circuit measurements, it is up to 83x faster and outperforms the near-Clifford simulator Clifft when more than about 25% of the gates are non-Clifford. With repeated sampling of each final state, its sampling rate per trajectory exceeds that of CUDA-Q by nearly five orders of magnitude. Our method also allows us to compare exact amplitude damping with its Pauli-twirled channel on a surface-code memory, revealing that twirling overestimates the detection rate by 21% and raises the logical error rate of a lookup decoder by 8%. This work makes exact, high-throughput simulation practical for general noisy circuits, from data generation for training decoders to studying measurement-based fault-tolerant protocols under realistic noise.

papers.title: Gravitational Form Factors and Transverse Mechanical Structure of the Charged Kaon in a Two-Fock-Sector Light-Front Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We study the electromagnetic and gravitational form factors of the charged kaon in a light-front Hamiltonian model with coupled $|u\bar s\rangle$ and $|u\bar s g\rangle$ Fock sectors. We solve the coupled Hamiltonian in a longitudinal Jacobi and transverse harmonic-oscillator basis, with the interaction strength fixed by the kaon mass. The momentum form factors are extracted from $T^{++}$, while the stress form factors are obtained from the transverse shear projection of the QCD Belinfante energy-momentum tensor, including diagonal, sector-changing, and constrained-field contributions. The strange antiquark carries the largest fraction of the kaon's longitudinal momentum, whereas the gluon carries only $2.05\%$. Despite this small momentum fraction, the gluon contributes $42.4\%$ of $|D_K(0)|$, for which we obtain $D_K(0)=-2.03610$. The charge and transverse momentum radii are $0.5178\pm0.0278\,\mathrm{fm}$ and $0.3394\pm0.0113\,\mathrm{fm}$, respectively, with uncertainties estimated from mass and basis variations. We obtain the transverse mechanical distributions using two ultraviolet continuations of the directly calculated $D$ form factors beyond $Q^2=2\,\mathrm{GeV}^2$. Both continuations give positive pressure at small transverse distances and negative pressure at larger distances. The corresponding transverse mechanical radii are $0.4616\pm0.0130\,\mathrm{fm}$ and $0.4768\pm0.0132\,\mathrm{fm}$, both larger than the transverse momentum radius. The central pressure changes substantially between the two continuations, whereas the pressure zero and mechanical radii vary much less.

papers.title: A structure-based model of the bacterial chemosensory array reveals how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes sensory responses
papers.abstract: We introduce a structure-based Ising model of the bacterial chemosensory array to investigate how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes signaling responses. The model couples the activity states of core signaling units and of CheW subunits within hexameric rings on a lattice with the structure observed in cryoEM experiments. Recent experiments show that increasing CheW participation in hexameric rings raises response cooperativity in non-adapting cells and sensitivity in adaptation-proficient cells. Our lattice model quantitatively reproduces both effects, while mean-field theory shows that CheW increases the effective coupling between core units, sharpening the response in both cell types. The statistics of CheW placement (complete hexameric rings versus random distribution) substantially alter how responses vary with CheW abundance. Moreover, different coupling strengths can yield the same static response yet markedly different activity fluctuations and dynamics. CheW abundance further controls a crossover from relaxational to oscillatory fluctuations, whose location depends on the spatial distribution of CheW. These dynamical signatures, including oscillations predicted near native CheW levels, are testable by single-cell dynamics measurements. Combined with CheW titration and our modeling results, these measurements can probe the array's assembly dynamics and allosteric couplings. Beyond the chemosensory array, our approach can generalize to other large protein complexes, providing a framework to study the functional role of scaffolding proteins and allosteric interfaces in signal processing.

papers.title: MetacouplingLLM: Integrating geographic adjacency, flow indicators, and LLM-assisted analysis
papers.abstract: The metacoupling framework examines interactions within coupled human and natural systems and between adjacent or distant systems, but its application is constrained by inconsistent geographic classifications and limited standardized quantitative workflows. We present MetacouplingLLM, an open-source Python package integrating adjacency databases, reproducible flow indicators, and large language model (LLM)-assisted qualitative analysis. The databases combine administrative boundaries, hydrography, and fixed-crossing evidence, with configurable adjacency policies and optional country-level maritime adjacency. Metacoupled Flow Shares, Metacoupled Flow Evenness, and the Metacoupled Flow Concentration Index characterize flow composition, balance across coupling types, and partner concentration within each type. The qualitative workflow combines literature retrieval, optional web evidence, and geographic checks to draft structured analyses. Applications to global marine fishing and Indonesian palm oil demonstrate these capabilities; the fisheries reanalysis reveals differing partner concentration among regions with similar telecoupled flow shares. MetacouplingLLM facilitates consistent framework application and comparative sustainability research.

papers.title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
papers.abstract: Contemporary classical information processors integrate tens of billions of transistors printed on a chip, yet are fully controlled through comparatively few external wires. This is possible because data flows through hard-coded operations in step with a global clock and is steered by external instructions. Today's solid-state quantum processors are different -- every qubit receives instructions from outside the chip via its own dedicated control line, and error correction adds a further torrent of syndrome data that is transported off-chip. Here we show that the external control of a quantum chip can be greatly simplified. We propose a fault-tolerant architecture for universal quantum computation, inspired by modern classical processors, in which quantum information flows through a fixed, clocked device, propelled by local gates in a planar array. Our quantum processor receives an input stream of classical instructions via a small, constant number of external wires, each attached to a single qubit. Except for those few qubits coupled to external wires, all qubits evolve under a periodically-applied geometrically-local depth-3 circuit, which is fixed at the time the device is fabricated. Assuming a noiseless global clock (so that every operation is applied on schedule, though imperfectly), we establish an accuracy threshold theorem: For physical noise below a universal threshold -- afflicting every gate, measurement, and wire -- a chip with $n$ physical qubits can run any quantum algorithm that uses~$n/{\sf polylog}(n/\epsilon)$ logical qubits, where $\epsilon$ is the error rate per logical gate. Each logical gate takes time~$n/{\sf polylog}(n/\epsilon)$; an alternative design, in which quantum operations remain strictly local and noisy, but on-chip wires broadcast noiseless classical signals instantaneously, reduces the time per logical gate to ${\sf polylog}(n/\epsilon)$.

papers.title: Molecular Kondo Ball Based on an Endohedral Fullerene
papers.abstract: We theoretically predict a molecular Kondo ball in TiSc$_2$N@C$_{80}$/Al(111), where a Ti-centered $S = 1/2$ local moment is encapsulated within a closed fullerene $\pi$ cage that serves as an itinerant-like electronic reservoir for Kondo screening. First-principles calculations show that intermediate molecule--substrate hybridization broadens the discrete C$_{80}$ molecular levels into itinerant-like electronic states while preserving the Ti local moment, with similar electronic conditions found for Cd(0001) and In(101).Hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) simulations reveal a temperature-dependent Fano resonance with a Kondo temperature of about 60 K.The key electronic characteristics underlying the Kondo state remain robust against adsorption orientation, demonstrating that the closed cage geometry provides an orientation-tolerant molecular architecture for Kondo screening.

papers.title: Vanguard: Knowing When to Trust the Draft in Speculative Vision-Language Agents
papers.abstract: Vision-language agents that browse websites, operate phones and act in homes reason before every action, so every step waits for a large model, a latency and cost that stand in the way of deployment. Step-level speculation lets a small model draft each step and calls the large model only on rejected drafts, but its outcome rests on the judge, and a judge that reads only a step's text cannot tell whether the step fits the screen it acts on. We find that a few samples of a small model can contain a correct step about as often as the large model gets the step right, and not always on the same steps: checked against the screen, small drafts can be not only cheaper but better. We present Vanguard, a training-free judge that leaves the draft and target models unchanged: a general decision model, with the screenshot in view, gives each candidate step a probability of being right in one forward pass; the best candidate is kept if it clears a threshold, and otherwise the large model writes the step. On web, mobile and embodied agents, a 2B draft judged by Vanguard is at least as accurate as its 8B target and significantly more accurate on Mind2Web and EB-ALFRED, while the target writes only a minority of the steps; it completes far more closed-loop episodes, and with a 27B target from another family it is both faster and more accurate. Vanguard is the most accurate judge we compare on the agent tasks; it relies on the screenshot on web and mobile tasks, its calibrated threshold transfers to unseen websites, and across model families its gain over the target grows with the draft's pass@4 relative to the target's accuracy. Vanguard composes with token-level speculative decoding and matches trained process reward models on mathematics, turning speculation from a way to save the large model's work into one that can improve on it.

papers.title: ReLoco: Unified Humanoid Locomotion and Fall Recovery via Behavior-Conditioned Motion Priors
papers.abstract: Humanoid robots must recover from falls and resume commanded motion to sustain locomotion. Learning these behaviors in one policy requires supervision that accommodates both upright movement and ground-contact recovery. We present ReLoco, a framework that uses behavior-conditioned adversarial motion priors to learn locomotion, get-up from arbitrary fallen postures, and command resumption within one proprioceptive policy. During training, robot posture selects the expert pool and conditions a shared discriminator with two behavior-specific outputs. Task rewards and shared regularization support command tracking and recovery, while temporary assistance facilitates exploration. A simulation-based refinement stage supplies robot-executed motion references for this supervision. Ablations examine conditional supervision, output separation, and reference quality under matched settings. At a common training iteration, the full policy achieves $96.80\%$ independent get-up success and $96.96\%$ push-recovery success, including command resumption. Its torso planar velocity root-mean-square error is $0.1266$~m/s, $14.7\%$ lower than the conditional single-output variant, with similar joint-angle discrepancy measured by dynamic time warping. Deployment on the 64.5-kg Tiangong~3.0 humanoid demonstrates walking, running, get-up, and locomotion resumption after falls using one proprioceptive actor, without controller switching or on-robot policy fine-tuning.

papers.title: Semi-Implicit and Convex Splitting Schemes for the Surface Cahn--Hilliard Equation on Curved Closed Surfaces
papers.abstract: The surface Cahn--Hilliard equation describes phase separation and coarsening of a conserved composition field on fixed curved surfaces. We study a mixed $hp$-surface finite element discretization with curvilinear high-order elements, primarily on the sphere, with the stabilized semi-implicit BDF2 integrator and a stabilized convex-splitting variant solved with the same factorization. For the semi-implicit scheme with a quadratic-growth potential and a truncated nonlinear bulk chemical-potential term, we prove exact discrete mass conservation, energy decay for the start-up steps, an exact per-step energy balance for the BDF2 phase, and a conditional monotone law for a modified Lyapunov functional. A manufactured solution with analytic forcing verifies second order in time and the expected $h$- and $p$-convergence. Torus tests include controlled equal-area bands, whose diffuse energies reproduce sharp-interface perimeters within $1\%$, deterministic coarsening, and a viscous R{\"a}tz--Voigt model. Genus-two and genus-three calculations on implicit surfaces conserve mass to roundoff, and their unstable-mode counts agree with area-based Weyl estimates within $1\%$.

papers.title: The Geometric Imprint of a Tilted Accretion Disk in Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: Gravitational wave astronomy has opened a new window onto black holes and the dynamics of strong-field gravity, while accretion flows offer a complementary and natural laboratory for probing strong-field physics. In this work, we show that the gravitational wave emission from an initially tilted accretion disk carries a distinct imprint of its orientation. We perform three dimensional general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations and evaluate the gravitational waves through Teukolsky equation. For an aligned disk, the emission is concentrated in low-$|m|$ modes, where $m$ is the azimuthal quantum number. For the initially tilted disk, higher-$|m|$ modes make a larger relative contribution. As the tilted flow subsequently aligns with the black hole spin, the contribution of $|m|\ge2$ modes decreases, showing strong correlation with the tilt angle. This indicates that the gravitational waves generated by the black hole environment carries geometric information about the surrounding matter. Our results establish a route towards using multimode gravitational radiation to probe the geometry and dynamical evolution of accretion flows in the strong-field region.

papers.title: Resilient Federated LQR over Noisy and Lossy Uplinks via Scalar Communication
papers.abstract: This paper studies model-free federated learning of a common LQR controller for a fleet of similar systems that communicate with a server over an uplink subject to limited bandwidth, packet dropout, and additive noise. We propose \textsc{ResiFedLQR}, a scalar communication scheme in which each agent sends one real number per packet, with redundancy, instead of full gradient estimates. The scalars can be gradient coordinates, projections of the gradient onto random directions reproduced at the server from a shared seed, or the rollout costs themselves. For the projection encoding, we prove that, with high probability, every iterate stabilizes all agents and the fleet-average cost converges linearly to a neighborhood of the optimum whose radius separates heterogeneity, sampling, and communication effects, and we derive a rule for choosing the number of transmissions from the channel parameters and the fleet size. We then compare the encodings with full-gradient transmission under the same uplink budget and identify the signal-to-noise regime and power constraint under which each is preferable. Numerical experiments on a heterogeneous fleet evaluate stability and convergence under varying noise levels and dropout probabilities.

papers.title: Time-Decay Rates toward a Rarefaction-Contact-Shock Composite Wave for the One-Dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations
papers.abstract: We consider the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations when the end states are connected by a rarefaction wave, a contact discontinuity, and a shock. For a fixed weak nonzero shock, sufficiently weak rarefaction and contact waves, and small H^2(R) initial perturbations, we establish asymptotic stability with a time-dependent shift on the viscous shock. The L^4 time average of the uniform perturbation and the shift velocity over [t,2t] is bounded by C_S(1+t)^(-1/4). We prove pointwise-in-time bounds of order (1+t)^(-1/12) on the whole line, (1+t)^(-1/4) near the shifted shock, and (1+t)^(-1/6) on |x| >= \eta t for each fixed \eta>0. The proof uses energy estimates and comparison on finite time interval

papers.title: Scalable Iterative Multi-Agent Path Finding under Turn Constraints
papers.abstract: Large-scale multi-mobile-robot systems require fast and reliable path planning under realistic motion constraints. Multi-Agent Path Finding with turn actions (MAPF$_T$) explicitly models orientation changes and turn-induced delays, but these constraints increase the computational burden of search-based methods. Priority-inheritance-based planning offers a highly scalable alternative, yet directly extending it to MAPF$_T$ is nontrivial because turn actions break the immediate node-vacation assumption underlying conventional priority inheritance. To address this challenge, this paper proposes PIBT$^*_T$, an efficient iterative solver for MAPF$_T$. PIBT$^*_T$ advances scalable multi-agent coordination by preserving the lightweight single-timestep planning mechanism of Priority Inheritance with Backtracking (PIBT), while introducing dedicated mechanisms to handle turn-induced dependencies, local deadlocks, livelock, and inefficient repeated pushing. Experiments on standard MAPF benchmarks show that PIBT$^*_T$ achieves high success rates and strong scalability, solving instances with up to 1000 agents within seconds. For realistic engineering environments, Action Dependency Graph (ADG)-based execution simulation and a flexible manufacturing system case study show that turn-aware planning better reflects robot execution and reduces actual makespan compared with classical MAPF planning. Experiments with TurtleBot4 robots further validate the practical feasibility of the proposed method.

papers.title: MLE Agents: Autonomous ML Engineering in Large-scale Recommendation Systems
papers.abstract: The typical workflow for improving large-scale ranking and recommendation models is slow and tedious: an engineer forms a hypothesis, implements it as a code change, trains a model, and evaluates it both offline and online, often relying on their own intuition and experience along the way. Autonomous LLM agents promise to speed this up by running the loop on their own, but it is still unclear whether they can do this in industry-scale systems rather than on benchmarks or small proxy tasks. We build human-on-the-loop machine learning engineer (MLE) agents that propose, implement, train, and evaluate model changes on large-scale search rankers. Engineers retain control over objective design, search direction, and final-model review. We identify three obstacles that make this industry setting challenging: feedback takes hours per experiment, offline metrics do not always predict online impact, and improvements saturate after the early wins. We address these with parallel training runs, an objective calibrated to match online impact, and careful context engineering. In one campaign, the system ran 1,097 completed candidate experiments and accepted 325, a 29.6\% acceptance rate compared with 15.6\% in the earlier campaign under a different objective and search constraint. Its best model increases search volume by 0.23\% in an A/B test of large scale. Several improvements were architectural changes the team had never tried, drawn from the broader industry and literature, suggesting that MLE agents can explore regions of the design space that human intuition overlooks. We find that the design of the harness around the model matters: intuition suggests that a stronger underlying model is enough, but in our experience, the design of the loop around it is just as critical. More broadly, our work shows that autonomous agents can do real machine-learning engineering in industry-scale systems.

papers.title: CoSlice: Coordinated Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for 5G Network Slicing Allocation
papers.abstract: Radio Access Network (RAN) slicing is a shared resource allocation problem: each slice seeks to satisfy its Service Level Agreement (SLA) with minimal radio-resource consumption, while all slices compete for a limited resource budget. This creates both an intra-slice trade-off between SLA assurance and resource efficiency and an inter-slice conflict over shared resources, calling for specialized yet coordinated control. In this work, we present CoSlice, a coordinated multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for inter-slice physical resource block allocation in Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN). CoSlice uses preference-conditioned slice agents for fast resource allocation and an LLM-based coordinator to adapt their objectives using global network observations at a slower timescale. We formulate the problem as a multi-objective partially observable stochastic game (mo-POSG), establish the existence of a Preference Correlated Equilibrium, and derive a sublinear regret bound for the learning procedure. We implement the algorithm by using a two-stage training procedure that consists of multi-objective pretraining and joint optimization. We build a network slicing evaluation environment using ORANSlice and its radio-frequency simulator (RFsim), supporting realistic protocol-stack execution and application traffic across multiple slices. Experimental results show that CoSlice reduces both average and tail SLA violations compared with other centralized and multi-agent baselines under diverse slice workloads.

papers.title: Training-Free Domain Generation for One-Shot Federated Learning with Server-Side Pre-trained Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: One-shot federated learning (OSFL) has attracted increasing attention for its ability to substantially reduce communication overhead by limiting client-server interaction to a single communication round. Nevertheless, this limited interaction makes learning from heterogeneous client distributions challenging.
