Furthermore, the physical regimes of complex nonlinear discharge transitions, including the alpha-gamma mode transition, local-to-nonlocal electron collisional heating mode transition and low-density jumps, are accurately mapped within the similarity space. Similarity transformations extend these boundaries across scales, opening a new avenue for rapid kinetic characterization and optimization of radio-frequency plasma sources.

papers.title: Synthetic Crystal Data Generation for Diffusion Pretraining in Material Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based pretraining has emerged as a powerful strategy for learning transferable representations in graph neural networks for materials property prediction without requiring quantum-mechanical labels such as energies, forces, and stresses for every pretraining structure. However, the method retains a critical dependency: it requires structures residing near local minima of a potential energy surface, which have traditionally been obtained through costly DFT relaxations of known or physically synthesized compounds. This reliance constrains both the scale and the structural diversity of available pretraining data, leaving large regions of crystal structure space unexplored. In this work, we connect diffusion-based pretraining with synthetic structure generation to reduce this bottleneck. We introduce a synthetic data generation pipeline combining three complementary strategies: perturb-and-relax, generative sampling via MatterGen, and protostructure enumeration. Where structural relaxation is required, we use fast machine-learned interatomic potentials instead of performing a new DFT relaxation for each generated structure. We further compare a coordinate-denoising control with continuous-time variance-preserving (VP) and sub-VP diffusion objectives using a randomly initialized Orb-v2 backbone. The source comparison covers seven MatBench property-prediction tasks, and an eighth task, \texttt{mp\_gap}, is included in the protostructure scaling study. Every synthetic-pretraining condition numerically outperforms random initialization on all seven source-comparison tasks. Scaling the protostructure corpus from 20k to 165k under a fixed 400-epoch schedule numerically matches or exceeds MP-20k pretraining on most tasks; because this protocol increases both data diversity and optimization updates, the result reflects joint data-and-compute scaling.

papers.title: A Hybrid Exact-Heuristic Solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation Problem
papers.abstract: We describe the solver we submitted to the second round of the SOICT 2026 contest on the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, a selective pickup-and-delivery routing problem with time windows, open routes and heterogeneous taxis. The solver is a single-file, standard-library Python program that combines (i) a constant-time insertion test based on latest-arrival slack, (ii) greedy insertion, local search and an Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) with simulated-annealing acceptance, and (iii) an exact route-selection engine that enumerates, for every taxi, the best feasible route for each request set and then solves the resulting set-packing problem by branch-and-bound strengthened with route-based large neighborhood search, Lagrangian bounds and reduced-cost fixing. The engine is chosen automatically from the instance size, and an independent verifier and a watchdog guarantee that a valid answer is always printed. On the official evaluation (38 scored instances, 5-minute limit) the solver obtained a total benefit of 487,237, finished every run within 277 s and used at most 279 MB; 28 of the 38 instances terminated well before the limit.

papers.title: Generalized Schrieffer-Wolff transformation
papers.abstract: The Schrieffer-Wolff transformation (SWT) is a cornerstone of effective-Hamiltonian theory. However, the SWT is predominantly used for weak-coupling problems, while a systematic counterpart for strongly coupled regimes remains largely unexplored. A general closed-form SWT generator and a clear physical principle for gauge fixing remain elusive, obscuring the transformation's underlying structure. We introduce the dual SWT to deal with the strong-coupling problems. The generalized SWT (gSWT) is formulated for any Hermitian operator and block partition. We establish the geodesic principle for its canonical gauge. Furthermore, we derive an exact closed-form solution of the gSWT generator at every order as a finite nested-commutator sum whose only input is the active gap set. Both the geometric and algebraic aspects of the SWT physics are revealed. The gSWT framework is illustrated in two quantum many-body models, the collective spin model and the transverse-field Ising model.

papers.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
papers.abstract: A language model is trained once and frozen. Making it better takes another training run, or a prompt, a harness or extra computation at inference that is gone once the task ends. We show a third way: to our knowledge for the first time, a language model rewrites its own weights by its own reasoning and becomes better, with no gradients and no training. We call this self-rewriting: the model is its own optimizer. In earlier work, a frontier model edited a much smaller one; here an open 27B model, given its weights, its graded answers and the ability to run itself, diagnoses its own failure and rewrites the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on problems it never saw. It keeps getting better: it tests its edits on practice problems and submits only what works, each edit improving on the last, and over eight consecutive sessions its accuracy only rises. It repairs a damaged copy of itself, like a broken robot that fixes itself without being rebuilt: the copy solves almost nothing, yet with no retraining and without ever reading the original weights, the model brings it back to over 80% of the original accuracy on image tasks it never saw. And the ability emerges with scale: in one model family, the smaller models make no edit or break themselves, and only the largest improves and repairs itself. Unlike test-time scaling, self-rewriting writes its gain into the weights, at no cost per answer; unlike training, it runs only forward passes, as serving does. The wall between training and inference is a limit of our tools, not a property of intelligence. We believe self-rewriting is a necessary step toward recursive self-improvement: a model that, like a human, does not separate training from inference could keep upgrading itself for life, with no larger model, no harness or prompt engineering, and no pre- or post-training.

papers.title: Simultaneous analysis of approximate leave-one-out cross-validation and mean-field inference II: General convex penalties
papers.abstract: For smooth penalties and group Lasso, Part I (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.02624) analyzed approximate leave-one-out (ALO) cross-validation by comparing its weights with the trace correction used in mean-field inference. For a $C^2$ penalty $R$, the matrix entering these corrections is $A=[\nabla^2R(\widehat b)+X^TDX]^{-1}$, where $\widehat b$ is the full-data estimator and $D$ is the diagonal matrix of fitted loss curvatures; for group Lasso, the penalty and loss curvatures are first restricted to the active support before taking the pseudoinverse. The obstacle to extending this argument to general convex penalties was the lack of an explicit formula for the matrix $A$ entering these corrections. For every finite-valued strongly convex penalty, we construct such a matrix from ordinary derivatives of the penalty response at the observed subgradient. Its projection--pseudoinverse formula separates the response space and penalty curvature, fixed by conditioning, from the explicit design dependence. This supplies the missing ingredient to extend the probabilistic argument of Part~I. The construction recovers the inverse Hessian for smooth penalties and the active-group inverse for group Lasso, including inactive boundary groups. In the proportional regime, for Gaussian designs with general positive-definite covariance and covariance-scaled strong convexity, we obtain unconditional bounds comparing both ALO and mean-field predictions with exact leave-one-out predictions in regression and single-index models. The expected average squared prediction error is $O(n^{-1})$, and the expected absolute criterion error is $O(n^{-1/2})$, under bounded, 1-Lipschitz loss scores and suitable test functions. The matrix and ALO weights use only observed data; the mean-field correction additionally uses the design covariance. The proofs are formalized in Lean~4.

papers.title: A Single-Shot Method for the Absolute Polarization Angle Calibration of CMB Telescopes with Artificial Sky Sources via Stellar Diffraction Encoding
papers.abstract: Absolute polarization angle calibration of cosmic microwave background (CMB) telescopes at the $\lesssim 0.1^\circ$ level is needed to prevent instrumental mixing of $E$ modes into $B$ modes from biasing constraints on primordial gravitational waves and cosmic birefringence. Artificial polarized sky sources like drones, balloons, or satellites can provide calibration references, but transferring their emitted polarization angle from the payload frame to the celestial frame remains a challenge. We propose a calibrator architecture, applicable to any such source, in which a single dual-use grid-optic sets the polarization axis of the emitted millimeter-wave signal and also diffracts starlight into a co-aligned star camera. The resulting diffraction spectra record the grid's orientation relative to the stars, so that it can be measured directly on the sky without fine alignment between the camera and grid-optic. We describe the geometry and physics of this concept and show that it significantly simplifies obtaining the calibration angle the observatory needs, because precise payload attitude is no longer needed and the received polarization is insensitive to small line-of-sight errors. In simulations of 1000 real star fields that include camera-grid misalignment, lens distortion, lateral chromatic aberration, atmospheric refraction, and stellar colors, a single exposure recovers the polarizing grid-optic's orientation in the celestial frame with an uncertainty of $\simeq 0.002^\circ$, fifty times below the $0.1^\circ$ goal. We also discuss the hardware tolerances a physical calibrator must meet, which future work will test. Our results establish the feasibility of this approach and motivate development of a dual-use grid-optic.

papers.title: Distrustful entanglement-based Quantum Key Distribution
papers.abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is the one of the most explored application of quantum information theory. While practical QKD systems are being deployed around the world, a major issue of these setups are that one has to trust the measurement devices of both parties. On the other hand, the most secure among such schemes are called device-independent (DI) QKD protocols, where no component of the setup is assumed to be trusted. However, due to their high technological demand, their loophole-free version currently remain out of practical reach. Inspired by the real world, we consider the traditional QKD in a distrustful measurement setting, that is, the measurement devices can only be trusted upto some level of confidence, which might still be large but not completely trusted. We then derive a general lower bound on the asymptotic key rate in this scenario. Then considering perfect detectors and source, and the entanglement-based BB84 (BBM) protocol, we show that to obtain secure keys one needs to trust their devices more than 92 %. However, we observe that such a protocol can not be realised with any level of distrust using the realistic detectors and sources at the current technology. Finally, we also consider the BBM protocol with arbitrary dimensional systems and observe that they are more robust to distrust than qubit systems. Consequently, with the same level of distrust, along with same detector and source efficiences, one can get better key rates with high-dimensional systems.

papers.title: The Impact of Seeding Threshold on Wandering Black Hole Populations and Merger Rates
papers.abstract: Cosmological simulations following massive black holes (MBHs) with dynamical friction subgrid models predict hundreds to thousands of off-centre, wandering MBHs in massive galaxies. We investigate how the wandering MBH population changes with halo mass seeding threshold. We present cosmological zoom-in simulations of a $(15\,\mathrm{cMpc})^3$ volume to $z=2$, using the halo mass seeding thresholds of ASTRID, EAGLE and Illustris-TNG $(5\times10^{9}-5\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h)$, with a fixed MBH seed mass of $m_\mathrm{seed}=2\times10^{6}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h$. The subgrid dynamical friction model for MBHs switches to accurate integration around MBHs using the \textsc{ketju} module above $m_{\bullet} \geq 2\times10^{7}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h$. We find that the seeding threshold greatly affects the MBH population: the number of seeded MBHs varies by a factor of ten and the number of wandering MBHs in the most massive galaxy ($M_\star=4.4\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) varies from 2 to 115. An MBH can become a wanderer in two ways. Interactions with other galaxies can offset a central MBH in low-mass galaxies ($M_\star\sim10^{8}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) if seeded in low mass halos $(\lesssim10^{10}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot/h)$. Alternatively, wandering MBHs can be added through mergers. The growth of the most massive MBHs is insensitive to the seeding threshold. While the total number of MBH mergers varies by an order of magnitude, the number of massive dynamically resolved MBH mergers differs by most a factor of $\sim3$ between seeding thresholds. The dynamically resolved binaries coalesce typically on timescales of $\sim10-250\,\mathrm{Myr}$ after becoming bound.

papers.title: Exact solution of the two-dimensional one-component plasma on the truncated Beltrami pseudosphere
papers.abstract: The two-dimensional one-component plasma, $N$ logarithmically interacting point charges in a neutralizing background, is solved exactly at coupling $\Gamma=2$ on the truncated Beltrami pseudosphere, the tractrix-generated surface of constant curvature $-1/a^2$, bounded by its rim and by a second parallel at meridian parameter $u=u_{\max}$. A conformal map takes the surface onto a flat cylinder, where the interaction is the flat-cylinder potential and the curvature enters only through the area element; the partition function is a product of incomplete gamma functions, the density is explicit and all correlations are determinantal. The thermodynamic limit is taken at fixed background density, with $u_{\max}$ fixed and $a\propto\sqrt{N}$, as on the sphere; the logarithmic interaction having no intrinsic length, this is equivalent to letting $N$ grow on a fixed surface. The free energy is obtained through the constant term, all coefficients in closed form: a bulk term proportional to $N$, the flat hard-wall surface tension times the total boundary length, and a shape-dependent constant, with no term in $\ln N$. This is the conformal-anomaly prediction for Euler characteristic zero, tested here with integrated Gaussian and boundary curvatures separately nonzero and cancelling; the model being a cylinder plasma with a specific axial potential, the expansion coincides term by term with the general result of Shen and Forrester, whose universal constants are the quadratures of the two boundary layers. At both walls the density tends to the flat contact value $n_b\ln 2$, from opposite sides, although their circumferences differ by a factor $\cosh u_{\max}$. Asymptotics are checked against the exact solution up to $N=4096$, and Monte Carlo simulations at $\Gamma=1$, 4 and 6, validated on the exact $\Gamma=2$ density, show how both boundary layers evolve with the coupling.

papers.title: Auditing Hyperstimulation at Scale in Child-Facing YouTube Videos
papers.abstract: Parents, pediatricians, and journalists have raised concern that child-facing videos are becoming increasingly stimulating (faster-paced, louder, and more visually dense), but this concern rests mostly on ad hoc observation rather than systematic measurement. We present a large-scale audit of hyperstimulation patterns, which we refer to as content-independent production choices, such as rapid cutting, that may place demands on children's developing cognitive and sensory processing capacities. Drawing on parents' Reddit discussions and developmental psychology, we develop computational metrics for 12 hyperstimulation patterns. We apply these metrics to 16,375 videos from 542 child-facing YouTube channels spanning 2015-2026. We found broad increases in stimulation over time, with cut rates rising across all five content categories. Nearly a quarter of the channels increased in at least one stimulation pattern over time. More stimulating videos also tended to receive more views, but the relevant stimulation patterns differed across content types.

papers.title: Rest-frame annihilation lines of $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs in 23,000 stacked galaxy clusters
papers.abstract: Weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) annihilation features were reported as a 43 GeV line in three Fermi-LAT galaxy clusters ($\mathtt{S}_3$), as triad $\{\gamma\gamma, \gamma Z,\gamma h\}$ lines from $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs in LAT data cross-correlated ($\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$) with western eROSITA X-rays, and as a nonad (combining three triads) of two cross-annihilating WIMPs in $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$. A blind scan of LAT 16.3-year data around 23,343 high-latitude clusters in their rest frames finds three triads, at 70 GeV ($2.8\sigma$ trial-corrected, henceforth), $72$ GeV ($1.3\sigma$; strengthening to $2.7\sigma$ if mass-fixed by $\mathtt{S}_3$, $4.0\sigma$ combined with $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ masked around the clusters, $5.7\sigma$ if also combined with $\mathtt{S}_3$), and 74-75 GeV: a triplet not only rare ($3.5\sigma$) but also forming a $\{70,74\}$ GeV nonad ($3.4\sigma$; strengthening to $4.0\sigma$, $4.6\sigma$, and $6.1\sigma$, respectively). The spectral features, robust in and out of the $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ region and $\mathtt{S}_3$ clusters, appear in all Galactic quadrants and only in the cluster rest frame (vanishing upon redshift rescaling or permutation), fade away from cluster centers, are absent from their surrounding stacked fields, and like $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ indicate intrinsic few $10^{-19}$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$ cross sections (uncorrected) across samples. All features are largely explained by cross-annihilating $69.7^{+0.4}_{-1.0}$ and $74.5^{+1.1}_{-0.6}$ GeV WIMPs.

papers.title: Adaptive Sparsity-Aware Projection-Assisted Spectral Embedding for High-Dimensional Noisy Data with Nonlinear Structures
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose SPASE, an adaptive, sparsity-aware, projection-assisted spectral embedding method for feature extraction from high-dimensional noisy data with underlying nonlinear structures and latent sparsity patterns. We first construct a data-driven projection that adapts to the hidden sparsity patterns and the signal-to-noise ratio, reducing noise-induced distortion of pairwise distances. We then apply kernel-based spectral embedding to the projected data to explore the underlying geometric structure. The key methodological contribution is an energy-based projection selection algorithm that is adaptive to the signal-to-noise ratio and sparsity of the signal representation, while mitigating the impact of noise. On the theoretical side, we show that the resulting embeddings converge to the eigenfunctions of an integral operator associated with the latent signal, and the method can remain effective when the signal-to-noise ratio is low. We demonstrate the empirical performance of the proposed method through simulation studies and real-data applications, showing improved accuracy in downstream tasks such as classification and clustering.

papers.title: Embedding Cosine Measures Text Length Before It Measures Homogenization
papers.abstract: Mean pairwise cosine similarity between transformer embeddings is a standard measure of whether online discourse is converging under generative AI. When the embeddings are mean-pooled outputs of an encoder never trained for sentence similarity, this measure mostly tracks text length. In 6.06 million Reddit comments, an uncentered DeBERTa-v3 measure had suggested that only conservative discourse broke toward homogeneity after late 2022. Truncating the same comments from 10 to 150 words raises their mean cosine by eight times the reported break. A placebo that swaps every comment for a random one of equal length reproduces 81% of the asymmetry, and a fixed-content simulation reproduces 78%. The leading principal direction carries 99.9% of raw DeBERTa homogeneity, and once length is handled the asymmetry disappears under every encoder. On 575,000 Stack Exchange answers the measure reports a post-ChatGPT homogenization of technical sites that the placebo fully reproduces, although answers grew longer. A census of 31 studies locates the risk where anisotropic encoders meet time-series or length-unequal designs. A reverse control on a well-known experiment shows that centering with renormalization can reverse a genuine effect. We propose a low-cost diagnostic protocol. Corrected measures show that the two political camps converged between 2019 and 2022 and stopped converging before ChatGPT. Cross-camp replies engage their targets more closely than same-camp replies.

papers.title: A Counterexample to Voiculescu's Normal Dilation Conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct a compact operator $T$ with trace class self-commutator and vanishing Helton-Howe measure such that $T\oplus S-M\notin \mathcal{S}_2$ for every bounded operator $S$ and every bounded normal operator $M$. This gives counterexamples to Voiculescu's normal dilation and stable classification conjectures. The construction uses magnetic shifts on finite square tori. Their real parts have commutators of uniformly bounded trace norm, while their frame errors admit logarithmic lower bounds in the lattice size. A summability criterion for frame error turns these finite-dimensional estimates into a compact counterexample. The same operator inequalities yield a rank profile invariant under Hilbert-Schmidt perturbations and normal stabilization, which distinguishes the example from zero.

papers.title: Jetriever: Shifting Agent Memory Retrieval from Similarity to Utility
papers.abstract: Whether a stored memory helps answer a user's question often depends on world knowledge rather than surface similarity. Jetriever replaces similarity search with full-pool utility scoring: given a query, it uses Jev, an LLM-derived System One decision model, to score every stored memory for the probability that it is useful to the answer, ranking the memory pool directly by those probabilities. On InMind's 125 indirect-query tasks, Jetriever places the gold exchange first in 84.8% of cases (versus 1.6% for BM25 and 0.0% for MiniLM with user-turn indexing) and reaches 76.0% end-to-end Application, compared with at most 16.0% across published retrieval and memory systems. A controlled 20-question comparison disentangles recognizing implicit evidence from ranking it properly: Jev and Qwen3.5-9B both recover 90% of gold exchanges within the top 50 (versus 30% for the BERT-based decision model Laya), yet at rank 1 Jev reaches 85% while Qwen3.5-9B drops to 40%. On a dimension-proportional random sample of 60 MemoryAgentBench questions, Jetriever raises the four-dimension average from 44.3% (ReFind) to 55.4%, at a mean retrieval cost of USD 0.00834 per InMind query and USD 0.03103 per MAB query. Together, these results show that effective utility retrieval hinges on combining broad world knowledge, calibrated ranking probabilities, and affordable full-pool evaluation.

papers.title: Randomization protects the average, not the trial: chance covariate imbalance and a calibration of balance $P$ values at the design stage
papers.abstract: Randomization makes the unadjusted treatment-effect estimate unbiased over the allocations a scheme could produce, although it does not balance any single trial. Chance imbalances on strongly prognostic baseline variables directly threaten the validity and regulatory credibility of trial results, yet what design-stage balance $P$ values imply for bias and error rates is seldom stated. We review evidence on chance covariate imbalance and derive that link under a linear model with one normal prognostic covariate, with simulation checks. Given the realized allocation, the unadjusted estimate is biased by $\beta$ times the difference in covariate means; in standard-error units the bias is $\rho Z_{\mathrm{bal}}$, where $\rho$ is the covariate-outcome correlation and $Z_{\mathrm{bal}}$ the balance z-statistic, so it does not shrink as trials grow. Pre-specified ANCOVA removes this bias, change scores reverse it, and non-collapsibility attenuates odds and hazard ratios even under perfect balance. A worst-balance threshold of $P = 1/e$ marks where the Sellke-Bayarri-Berger bound reaches 1; under complete randomization the worst of $k$ independent balance $P$ values falls below it with probability $1-(1-1/e)^k$, 0.99 for $k=10$. Any balance $P$ value $\geq 0.317$ keeps the two-sided conditional type I error of the unadjusted test at or below 5% for every $\rho$; at $1/e$ the one-sided error in the favoured direction is at most 4.1%, against 13-33% at $P = 0.05$. Design-stage balance scores should be benchmarked against complete randomization, weighted by external prognostic strength, and reported alongside allocation predictability and a pre-specified covariate-adjusted analysis plan.

papers.title: Exploring the link between predictive uncertainty and the sim-to-real gap in deep learning models utilizing synthetic data
papers.abstract: Today, state-of-the-art methods for quality control (QC) are based on Machine Vision, combining deep learning (DL) models with camera-based inspection. Yet, the integration of such solutions in industrial applications is often impeded by data sparsity and trust in model reliability. While synthetic data offers a promising approach to generate the necessary data with perfect annotations, it poses risks related to performance degradation due to the possible occurrence of the sim-to-real gap. This study conducts experiments using the ensemble method to estimate the predictive uncertainty of DL models trained on synthetic data. The results show that predictive uncertainty increases under the sim-to-real domain shift. However, the observed performance drop is dominated by a systematic sim-to-real bias rather than by ensemble disagreement.These findings contribute to the effective utilization of synthetic data in industrial settings while highlighting the importance of risk assessment for the deployment of DL solutions for QC tasks.

papers.title: A description of the space with no separable quotient presented by OpenAI
papers.abstract: OpenAI recently presented a remarkable solution to the longstanding separable quotient problem in Banach space theory. The result establishes its independence from ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal. Under the continuum hypothesis, the paper constructs a nonseparable Banach space $X$ with no separable infinite-dimensional quotient. The present paper offers an alternative exposition of the mechanism leading to $X$ and its properties. Our aim is to make the methods and results more accessible and to offer a clearer understanding of this exotic space.

papers.title: Constant-Factor Matching-Size Estimation in Random-Order Streams
papers.abstract: We give a one-pass algorithm that estimates the maximum matching size of an arbitrary simple graph within a constant factor using $O(\log^2 n)$ bits of space. The edges arrive exactly once in uniformly random order. The algorithm succeeds with probability at least $2/3$, does not require the number of edges in advance, and has worst-case total running time $O((m+1)\log(n+2))$ on a word RAM. Kapralov, Khanna, and Sudan (SODA 2014) obtained a polylogarithmic approximation in polylogarithmic space. Kapralov, Mitrovi\'c, Norouzi-Fard, and Tardos (SODA 2020) subsequently gave a constant-factor approximation from independent uniform edge samples and an $O(\log^2 n)$-approximation in random order. We obtain a constant factor in the latter model with the same $O(\log^2 n)$ space bound. The main ingredient is a comparison between the memory states of a recursive sampling algorithm under sampling with and without replacement. We account jointly for the sampled edges retained by the recursion and the positions at which they arrived. Randomized thresholds limit the additional information stored in numerical counters. A bound on the expected work of the entire recursion then removes the loss from its logarithmic depth. The resulting estimator repeatedly improves a coarse estimate while storing only one recursion stack.

papers.title: Low-energy states of a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain connected perpendicularly to a metallic lead
papers.abstract: Recently, Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains (SSHCs) coupled to metallic leads have attracted attention. In particular Mart\'{\i}nez {\it et al.} [Phys. Rev. Res. {\bf 8}, 043118 (2026)] studied a topological SSHC connected at one of its ends perpendicularly to a metallic lead modeled by a tight-binding chain. Here, we extend their results by incorporating the finite-size splitting of the end modes of the isolated SSHC, which are determined analytically with high accuracy. We also derive simple analytical expressions, valid in the low-energy regime, for the zero-temperature conductance through the lead and the relevant spectral densities. We find that, when the chemical potential coincides with that of the half-filled SSHC, the conductance reaches its maximum value, equal to that of the lead in the absence of the SSHC. By contrast, the conductance vanishes when the chemical potential is shifted by an amount equal to half the end-mode splitting.

papers.title: Generalized Limits of Finitely Additive Measures on Locally Compact Groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathscr{E}$ be an increasing family of Borel subsets of a locally compact topological group $G$ and let $\mu$ be a nonnegative finitely additive $\sigma$-finite measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $G$ whose values on $\mathscr{E}$ are finite but unbounded. Applying a generalized limit pointwise to the net of measures $\left\{B\mapsto\frac{\mu(B\cap E)}{\mu(E)}\right\}_{E\in \mathscr{E}}$ yields a finitely additive measure $\varphi_\mu$, which can be viewed as a generalized normalization of $\mu$ to total mass one. To obtain a nontrivial necessary condition on $\mu$ for the resulting measure $\varphi_{\mu}$ to be invariant, we establish two results of independent interest: we extend the Yosida--Hewitt decomposition to finitely additive $\sigma$-finite measures and prove a theorem previously stated by Bingham and Ostaszewski concerning translates of sets of Haar measure zero. The first theorem yields a decomposition of $\mu$ into a purely finitely additive component and two countably additive components, respectively singular and absolutely continuous with respect to Haar measure. Using the second result, we show that the invariance of $\varphi_\mu$ implies that the singular component $\mu_s$ is negligible relative to $\mu$ and can be removed without changing $\varphi_\mu$. A counterexample demonstrates that the purely finitely additive component $\mu_p$ need not have these properties.

papers.title: ASDL: A Fast Vector Approximation Algorithm for Multiplierless Designs of Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Matrix multiplications are one of the main computational bottlenecks in neural networks. The calculation reduces to numerous sums of partial products, which scale with the total number of Signed Power of Two (SPT) values in the multiplier matrix. Minimizing the SPT count can significantly reduce the computational burden. In this context, we present a Sum Of (signed) Powers Of Two (SOPOT) vector approximation algorithm that limits SPT counts, namely the Accelerated Signed Digit Loading (ASDL) algorithm. This approximation algorithm converts ResNet50 10 times faster than its predecessor MPGBP, while being more precise. We apply this method to the pre-trained coefficients of different convolutional neural networks, achieving 80.41\% ImageNet accuracy down from 81.3\%, at an average of only 1.5 active bits per coefficient. This is done without any retraining or calibration, which are typically required for the most aggressive quantization methods. Our approach offers a promising direction for neural network inference with higher energy efficiency and fewer hardware requirements: we anticipate up to 10 times improvement over bfloat16 inference.

papers.title: Beyond Family Labels: A Taxonomic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Prior for Avian 3D Shape Recovery
papers.abstract: Recovering 3D pose and shape of birds from single images is bottlenecked by the long tail of avian diversity: out of ~10,000 species, only a few dozen have 3D-labeled training data, and in-the-wild test sets routinely contain species never seen at training. Generalizing across clades is therefore a central problem. The current state of the art, AniMer+, mitigates it with a family-level contrastive loss that conveys only a binary same-family indicator per pair and discards the continuous structure of the species tree. We propose a taxonomic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck prior on the shape code of the AVES parametric bird mesh model: a multivariate Gaussian whose covariance decays exponentially with Linnaean rank distance, with a learnable selection strength and noise scale. The prior generalizes family contrastive into a continuous, generative form, exposing the graded cross- and within-family similarity that a binary indicator cannot, and brings continuous comparative phylogenetics in as a biology-grounded inductive bias for the long tail. Our method improves over AniMer+ on both metrics of the unseen-species CowBird benchmark and on CtrlAVES3D, while remaining comparable on seen-species CUB. A permutation ablation isolates taxonomic structure from generic Gaussian smoothing, and a rank-granularity ablation identifies cross-order distinctions (the structure beyond a family-vs-not indicator) as the dominant source of the unseen-species gain.

papers.title: Dynamical theory of the East model. I. A review on the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism
papers.abstract: The East model is a paradigmatic kinetically constrained spin model in one dimension that exhibits glassy dynamics. This review surveys the progress on the theoretical description of the dynamics of the East model, focusing on the spin time correlation function and the relaxation time. We summarize rigorous results on the super-Arrhenius scaling of the relaxation time in the low-temperature limit. We then present a unified derivation of the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism for both the fluctuation and domain bases. Within this formalism, an infinite hierarchy of coupled equations for the time correlation function and memory kernels emerges---a structure reminiscent of generalized mode-coupling theory developed for supercooled liquids. We review the analytical approximations obtained by truncating or closing the hierarchy at first or second orders and compare them against Monte Carlo simulations. Although these approaches perform reasonably at moderate temperatures, they universally fail in the low-temperature regime: mode-coupling closure schemes in the fluctuation basis introduce spurious ergodicity-breaking transitions, while truncations in the domain basis discard slower modes and fail to capture the asymptotic divergence of the relaxation time. The loss of analytical tractability beyond second order remains the central obstacle, underscoring the fundamental difficulty of describing hierarchical relaxation even in this ``simplest'' model of glassy dynamics.

papers.title: Orbital decomposition and evolution of LEGA-C-like galaxies in IllustrisTNG from z = 1 to z = 0
papers.abstract: Stellar orbits encode the dynamical history of galaxies and provide a physically motivated link between galaxy structures and assembly processes. Although orbit-based decompositions are well established in the Local Universe, their evolution across cosmic time, especially at higher redshifts, remains poorly explored. We investigate the orbital structure of \texttt{LEGA-C-like} galaxies in the \texttt{TNG100} simulation from $z=1$ to $z=0$ to identify how stellar mass, star formation activity, environment, merger history, gas content, and ex situ stellar mass growth shape their orbital transformation. We decomposed the stellar orbital structure of simulated galaxies into cold, warm, hot, and counter-rotating (CR) components using time-averaged orbital circularities. We find a strong mass dependence of orbital structure at $z=0$ as well as at $z=1$. Galaxies below $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)\sim11.2$ have a combined warm and cold orbital fraction of $\sim70\%$, whereas more massive systems have a hot-orbit fraction of $\sim60\%$. These trends are consistent with assembly pathways driven predominantly by wet and dry major mergers, respectively. Tracking the same galaxies to $z=0$ reveals a systematic, but mass-dependent, evolution toward lower rotational support: At both low and high stellar masses, the hot-orbit fraction increases, whereas the relative change is greater in low-mass galaxies. The survival of cold structure depends strongly on the star formation state at $z=1$; star-forming progenitors retain substantially larger cold fractions than the quiescent progenitors. At both redshifts, the orbital fractions show a rise (decline) in hot and CR (cold and warm) orbits with the ex situ stellar mass fraction at a fixed stellar mass. These results provide the first evolutionary framework for interpreting orbit-based decompositions of galaxies at the \texttt{LEGA-C} epoch.

papers.title: CIRT: Calculus of Inductive Refinement Types
papers.abstract: Refinement types are a powerful mechanism for statically verifying properties of programs. They have been successfully integrated into practical languages such as Haskell, Scala, and Rust. However, their metatheory is not yet fully understood. In this paper we present the first semantic model for a refinement type system that supports the full feature combination of subtyping, SMT-style equality, impredicative polymorphism, and (stratified) inductive types. Interactions between these features have led to inconsistencies in the past, and existing formalizations of refinement type systems omit at least one of them. We present a realizability model based on partial equivalence relations (PERs) over a Scott domain, which overcomes these obstacles. We use our model to prove the consistency of a core refinement type system and to give a semantic account of the annotation-independence property of refinement types. Our semantics uses two interpretations: a refined one, which interprets types and their refinements as PERs; and an unrefined one, consisting of complete uniform PERs with a bottom element (CUPERs), which models computational behaviour independently of refinements. We extend the model to positive and stratified inductive types, showing that both are consistent in the presence of impredicativity.

papers.title: Auditing World-Model Explanations in Retail Forecasting: Faithfulness, Accuracy and Price Response
papers.abstract: Forecasting models that read the price and promotion plan explain each forecast as a baseline, what would sell with nothing planned, plus the lift the plan adds, and merchants order stock and plan promotions on that lift. We show that an explanation can pass the checks used to trust it and still be wrong enough to cost money. We define eight checks for any forecaster that states a plan lift, six with a pass rule fixed before any result, and run them on a world model and on LightGBM. In generated store data with known effects, the world model passes the checks of construction, stability, price direction and agreement with sales and with LightGBM, yet when merchants plan into high-demand weeks it states 1.33 to 1.40 times the true lift, and 1.23 to 1.42 times in eight variants of that world; LightGBM overstates it too (1.26, and 1.16 to 1.35). Both still pick the right weeks to promote, but stock ordered to the world model's lift is off by 0.44 to 0.48 of the true lift. The world model's stated response to a lasting regular-price change is 4.7 to 6.5 times the true -0.5, an error in kind that only a measured cause finds. Sanity checks for explanations test whether an explanation depends on the model; a decision needs to know whether it is right about the world, and these results show the first does not give the second. For the final tuned world models of our companion paper on nine data sets, baseline and lift add up under each model's own plan on every window, but a deeper price cut lowers the forecast in 29% to 83% of item-week steps on Dominick's. Across 703 configurations from the settings searches, checks passed were not related to accuracy (Spearman 0.02, 95% interval -0.02 to 0.05). A noisy benchmark of price episodes in Dominick's data is reported as a check of direction only.

papers.title: Regularizing Treatment Leakage for LLM-based Uplift Estimation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide semantic features for uplift estimation, but treatment-revealing text can induce prediction shortcuts that do not transfer to deployment. We propose LLM-based Uplift Leakage Regularization (LULR) to address this risk. With the LLM encoder frozen, LULR penalizes dependence between the causal head's trainable shared representation and treatment while retaining separate outcome heads. The penalty uses a variational approximation to the contrastive log-ratio upper bound (CLUB) of mutual information, targeting treatment dependence rather than generic parameter shrinkage. Controlled proxy experiments provide exploratory evidence of improved ranking scores under injected treatment information relative to no regularization and the tested weight-decay setting. Structured-only benchmarks show modest, dataset-dependent effects. On an industrial pricing randomized controlled trial, mean offline lift@0.3 is 0.258 for LULR, compared with 0.106 for the same-backbone baseline. A separate one-week online A/B test of the complete deployed pricing policy records 5.45% higher sales volume and 1.91% higher gross merchandise value than the control arm. These short-term policy-level gains do not isolate the regularizer's effect.

papers.title: Social Welfare and Equilibrium in Distributed Microgrid Prosumer Coordination Under a Mixed Competitive-Cooperative Setting
papers.abstract: Price-based distributed prosumer coordination in distribution networks is fundamentally challenging when the aggregator pursues grid-level goals that couple prosumers' decisions, because the Lagrangian fails to separate and nodal prices are undefined under conventional dual decomposition. This paper develops a novel method that embeds mixed competitive-cooperative objectives exactly into prices, which are split into energy, congestion, and grid-objective components, closing the gap between the social welfare optimum and the competitive equilibrium. To compute the equilibrium, a distributed optimization algorithm is developed based on the projected Arrow-Hurwicz-Uzawa scheme. Explicit step-size rules are developed for the algorithm to guarantee $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{L})$ and $\mathcal{O}(1/L)$ ergodic convergence rates. Simulations on an IEEE 33-bus feeder that is connected to prosumers and electric vehicle fleets validate the accuracy and efficacy of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Decomposition Bounds for MCMC with Mixture Targets: Multimodality and Heavy-Tailedness
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative mixing-time bounds for Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms targeting multimodal and heavy-tailed mixtures. The dynamics of a Markov chain are decomposed into local and global levels, and possibly weak Poincar\'{e} inequalities at both levels are combined to form convergence bounds. We apply this framework to location and scale mixtures of strongly log-concave distributions, obtaining explicit convergence bounds for random-walk Metropolis, proximal, and random-scan Gibbs samplers. For location mixtures connected along a finite path, the bounds depend polynomially on the number of components and exponentially on neighboring separation, remaining informative as the overall diameter grows. For scale mixtures, we relate the global dynamics of the chain to the isoperimetry of the log-scale mixing distribution, and illustrate the effect of heavy-tailed targets by examining inverse-gamma mixing distributions.

papers.title: Signs of Wear: Evaluating Intelligent Speed Assistance Under Synthetic Adverse Conditions
papers.abstract: Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA) systems rely on cameras to recognize speed-limit signs, yet existing benchmarks underrepresent the weathered, dirty, and overgrown signs commonly encountered on rural roads. We use generative image editing to introduce different forms of wear into real street-level images of speed-limit signs. The resulting ISA-Wear dataset contains paired original and edited images. Guided by text instructions, a multimodal image-editing model adds snow, rust, vegetation, faded paint, or mud to the speed-limit sign in a street-level frame at three severity levels. Where appropriate, the surrounding scene is adapted as well, and the viewpoint is kept. Every edited frame has an unedited counterpart, and we only evaluate frames whose original is recognized correctly, so any failure can be attributed to the wear. Since the model alters the sign's geometry in 21\% of the edits, all edits are filtered by a geometric check and a manual review. Severity is measured as the LPIPS distance between the original and the edited sign plate. On 716 worn frames, we find that in detect-then-read pipelines, wear breaks detection before it breaks reading. The detector finds only 62\% of the worn signs, even though it finds every one of them in the original frames. Missed detections account for 78--87\% of failed reads, a pattern that a zero-shot detector shares. Given the annotated sign box, as in the crop-based benchmarks, a classifier still reads 78\% of the worn signs, but only 56\% when it has to rely on the detector

papers.title: BlockAlign: Preference Optimization for Trajectory-Distilled Video Generation
papers.abstract: Directly aligning trajectory-distilled video generators slashes rollout costs and optimizes the deployed few-step model without teacher fine-tuning or re-distillation. However, conventional flow-matching preference objectives assume single-head local velocity supervision, mismatching the finite-interval, block-average transition interface of trajectory-distilled generators such as Parallel Decoding Distillation (PDD) and Parametric Trajectory Distillation (PTD). Naively supervising individual unfused sub-interval velocity heads across all sub-steps rather than the fused block-average velocity at block starts (DirectAlign) induces a severe training--inference mismatch that degrades preference below the unaligned baseline. We introduce BlockAlign, an interface-consistent preference optimization framework that constructs states at valid block boundaries, queries the fused block-level velocity predictor, and supervises span-normalized transition residuals---seamlessly supporting DPO-, NFT-, and rollout-style objectives while preserving the native few-step sampler. We further build a unified post-training pipeline integrating offline pairs, reward-free semi-online continuations, and online rollouts with hierarchical preference selection and objective-aware block scheduling. Experiments on multi-reference video generation across MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA and an in-house model RefVid-V4 show that BlockAlign consistently outperforms unaligned distilled models and DirectAlign in structural plausibility, reference consistency, and visual quality. Notably, our approach unlocks PDD's 5x few-step rollout speedup for 3x faster end-to-end online training, achieving statistically significant human preference gains over PDD baselines (54.0% vs. 33.3% wins/losses, or 61.8% non-tie win rate on RefVid-V4; 51.3% vs. 34.7%, or 59.7% non-tie win rate on MiniMax-H3) and up to an 82.7% win rate against DirectAlign.

papers.title: Pair Correlation Conjecture for the Zeros of Artin $L$-functions I: Simple and Critical Zeros
papers.abstract: In 1973, Montgomery posed the pair correlation conjecture (PCC) for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Motivated by PCC, Montgomery conjectured that the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function are almost surely simple, and proved that at least $2/3$ are simple assuming the Riemann hypothesis (RH). In 1978, Mueller and Gallagher were able to prove asymptotically $100\%$ are simple assuming PCC and RH. Recently, Goldston et al. noticed that the assumption of RH can be removed in Mueller and Gallagher's method. In fact, assuming PCC by itself without RH is sufficient to prove that asymptotically $100\%$ of the nontrivial zeros are both simple and on the critical line. We adapt the notion of horizontal multiplicity from Goldston et al. to show that the nontrivial zeros of Artin $L$-functions attached to irreducible linear representation of the Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ are almost surely simple and lie on the critical line without assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH). We will assume the appropriate version of PCC along with some other widely believed conjectures.

papers.title: Up or down at every integer: Collatz-type maps of arbitrary sets and the up-down graph
papers.abstract: For a set $S$ of positive integers let $T_S$ send $x$ to $\lceil 3x/2\rceil$ if $x\in S$ and to $\lceil x/2\rceil$ otherwise. The odd numbers give the Collatz map, the even numbers give it again after a shift by one, and $S=\mathbb{N}$ gives Mahler's map $x\mapsto\lceil 3x/2\rceil$. All these maps are subgraphs of the up-down graph $G$, in which every $x$ has the edges $x\to\lceil x/2\rceil$ and $x\to\lceil 3x/2\rceil$, and so are the families of maps in which the direction is forced at some numbers and free at the others. The cycles of the maps are the simple cycles of the subgraph, their divergent orbits are its rays, and all maps of a family are bounded exactly when the subgraph has no ray. We classify the simplest sets and show that density says little: some sets of density one send every orbit to 1, and some periodic sets of arbitrarily small density have increasing orbits. Every positive integer is the least element of a cycle of some map. The critical proportion of steps up is $\log_3 2$: cycles stay below it, divergent orbits stay above it, and both come arbitrarily close. For sets periodic modulo a power of 2, an effective up-frequency from a finite Markov chain takes the place of the density, and a finite computation can prove that every orbit reaches a cycle. Mahler's Z-number problem is implied by a question about one such map. Finally, we ask how far the Collatz map is from maps whose behaviour can be proved. Finite changes never help. Adding fewer than $\log_{3/2}N+1$ even numbers below $N$ makes an orbit increase, while removing the odd numbers congruent to 9 or 15 modulo 16, an eighth of all integers, gives a map all of whose orbits provably reach the cycle (1,2); removing 22 residue classes modulo 512, a proportion 0.043, also suffices.

papers.title: Faster $\chi^2$ periodogram: Accelerating linear algebra with fast Toeplitz solvers
papers.abstract: In recent years, the traditional Lomb--Scargle periodogram, relying on least-squares fitting of a sinusoid to data with a known mean, has been mostly superseded by its floating-mean extension---the generalized Lomb--Scargle periodogram---due to the superior robustness and accuracy of the latter. While further generalization to higher-degree trigonometric polynomials (known as the multiharmonic analysis of variance and the fast $\chi^2$ periodogram) has been known for decades, its usage remains relatively uncommon, mostly due to its significantly higher computational cost. Here we present a technique reducing the computational complexity of such an extension by combining a Toeplitz formulation of the system of normal equations with non-uniform fast Fourier transforms, coupled with condition-number monitoring to protect against numerical instability. When modified for practical efficiency rather than asymptotic computational complexity, our approach reaches speed-ups exceeding an order of magnitude over current state-of-the-art implementations across a wide range of hyperparameters when evaluated on multithreaded systems, while matching or exceeding their accuracy. Additionally, we provide a reference implementation used for benchmarking, along with the code used to generate the results presented in this work.

papers.title: Characterizing nonlocal Sobolev spaces as generalized Bessel potential spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study nonlocal Sobolev spaces $H^{\rho,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $p \in (1,\infty)$, defined via a general class of nonlocal gradients $D^\rho$ associated with a kernel function $\rho$. As our main contribution, we establish three new equivalent characterizations of these spaces. First, we describe $H^{\rho,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ in terms of Fourier multipliers involving the symbol of the nonlocal potential associated with $D^\rho$. Second, we give a thorough functional analytic treatment of the nonlocal $\rho$-Laplacian $\Delta^\rho$, which allows us to represent general nonlocal Sobolev spaces through its square root $(-\Delta^\rho)^{1/2}$. Third, we show that $H^{\rho,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ coincides with the image $g_\rho * L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for a suitable convolution kernel $g_\rho \in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, which confirms that these spaces are genuine potential spaces. These results generalize the well-known fact that, in the special case of the Riesz kernel, the resulting fractional Sobolev spaces coincide with the classical Bessel potential spaces. In this spirit, the present work can also be viewed as introducing a natural notion of generalized Bessel potential spaces.

papers.title: CiGS: Conduction in Gaussian Splats for Interior Temperature Field from Thermal Images
papers.abstract: We present a method for inferring the interior temperature distribution of a solid object from registered multi-view visible-spectrum and thermal images, even when the thermal views cover only part of its surface. We formulate steady-state heat conduction as a Laplace boundary value problem and solve it with a direct boundary integral equation discretized over a point cloud: a Gaussian reconstruction of the visible-spectrum images supplies the boundary geometry, and the thermal images supply the boundary data. We do not build surface or volume meshes at any stage in our method. Instead, we sample collocation points from rendered depth without the pixels at depth discontinuities, and use a density subtraction that keeps the interior evaluation accurate up to the surface. The whole chain is differentiable, and we use it to recover the pose and depth of heating pipes, insulation defects, and the shape of cracks from thermal images. We validate our method through experiments on boundary value problems with Dirichlet-only and mixed Dirichlet and Robin boundaries, using synthetic and real captured data on scenes with challenging topology. These experiments show that our method matches analytical solutions and has better accuracy than FEM solvers.

papers.title: Global dynamics of large smooth solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system with Navier-slip boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions containing vacuum to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with bulk viscosity depending on the density, in smooth bounded connected domains, subject to the Navier-slip boundary conditions. Without any restriction on the size of initial data, we obtain time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponentialconvergence to equilibrium in Sobolev spaces for the density and velocity. Moreover for strictly positive initial density, uniform positivity and exponential decay of density gradients and second velocity derivatives are established. In contrast, if an initial vacuum occur, then it will persist and force the exponential growth of density gradients.

papers.title: Markets for Compute and Inference: Structure, Financing, and Risk Transfer
papers.abstract: Capacity to run large language models is rented by the accelerator-hour, and their output is sold by the million tokens. Both goods now have published price indices, an over-the-counter forward has traded on one, compute futures are listed offshore, and CME and ICE have specified futures on rental indices that await the United States regulator. We ask what in these two markets can be hedged, by whom, and at what price. Three findings stand out. First, the price that exchange contracts settle on is not the price that drives operators' revenue. The contracts on CME and ICE reference published short-dated rental rates, while most revenue, and with it credit quality, comes from private multi-year contracts whose prices are largely undisclosed. Second, the token price and the rental rate are linked by an identity through throughput and margin, but they are different exposures, so a hedge on the rental rate does not hedge the cost of inference; at the measured capability of GPT-5 the cheapest list price fell by a factor of 17 in twelve months, and by far less at lower capability. Third, the demand for hedging already sits in credit agreements, as the years by which operators' debt outlives their contracted revenue. Filings cannot measure that gap, because debt is scheduled year by year while contracted revenue rarely is, and the one loan that prices it settles the risk by cash prepayment against a model only the parties see. We design a reverse convertible note through which leveraged operators could buy protection against falling rental rates. Its coupon depends steeply on the annualised volatility of the rental rate, which the two public indices put between about 5% and 89% according to how each is built and the horizon measured; across that range the fair one-year coupon runs from 4.1% to 31.6%.

papers.title: Iso-Multiplication Modules over Noncommutative Rings: Triangular Classification and Rational Rigidity
papers.abstract: A right A-module M is called iso-multiplication if for every submodule N of M there is a two-sided ideal B of A such that N ?A MB. We construct noncommutative examples of isomultiplication modules which are not multiplication modules, including triangular algebras of arbitrary dimension. We classify all iso-multiplication modules over T_2(k) without a finitegeneration assumption. For a semiprime right Goldie ring we prove that the classical localization of an iso-multiplication module is multiplicity-free. Further consequences address composition length and local rings; we distinguish these from standard Morita, Ore-localization, and chaincondition results.

papers.title: ReactBench-AD: Do Driving VLAs and World-Action Models React to Imminent Hazards in Their Path?
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) and World-Action Models (WAMs) have emerged in autonomous driving with the promise of strong generalization to long-tail scenarios. Although these models achieve state-of-the-art results on autonomous driving benchmarks, most existing benchmarks are dominated by nominal scenarios and therefore cannot test this promise. To test one such long-tail capability that is critical for safety, we introduce ReactBench-AD, a benchmark that measures how driving models react to objects that appear in the ego vehicle's path. Built on real NAVSIM and PhysicalAI-Autonomous-Vehicles scenes, ReactBench-AD composites a crossing pedestrian, a standing pedestrian, or a stationary car consistently across all camera views and history frames. Each edited scene thus forms an exact, pixel-level counterfactual pair with its original, which allows us to isolate the causal effect of the inserted object on the predicted trajectory. Evaluating four VLAs and two WAMs, we find that they react weakly, often barely at all. Finally, we test how easily one of the evaluated VLAs, ReCogDrive, can be taught to brake hard for imminent hazards: a short fine-tuning stage on edited scenes substantially improves its reactions, with the learned behavior generalizing to unseen objects and fully real scenes, at minimal cost to nominal driving. These results call into question the out-of-the-box long-tail capabilities of these models, but suggest that they can be a strong foundation for acquiring them with little additional training, highlighting the value of real or synthetic data that demonstrates the long-tail behaviors nominal datasets rarely contain.

papers.title: Twister After Dark: Diagnosing a Damaging Nocturnal Tornado in Iloilo, Philippines (08 August 2026)
papers.abstract: At ~1430 UTC (2230 LST) on 08 August 2026, a significant tornado struck the Mandurriao and Jaro districts of Iloilo City, Philippines. Its parent supercell developed within the southwest monsoon enhanced by Typhoon Dolphin, under weak synoptic forcing, as a nocturnal low-level jet of ~40 kt near 1.5-3 km advected warm, moist marine air onshore. ERA5 depicted MUCAPE of ~2000 J kg$^{-1}$, negligible inhibition, an LCL below 300 m, and nearly purely streamwise low-level vorticity, but deep-layer shear (DLS, 0-6 km bulk wind difference) below 3 m s$^{-1}$. Hodographs from the newly operational Iloilo S-band dual-polarization radar (S-ILO), ~5-7 km from the storm, revealed low-level shear (LLS, 0-1 km bulk wind difference) of ~16 m s$^{-1}$ and 0-1 km storm-relative helicity of 124-211 m$^2$ s$^{-2}$. The storm exhibited a hook echo with a weak echo hole, a $Z_{DR}$ arc and ring, an elevated 55-60 dBZ rear-flank core consistent with a descending reflectivity core, and a ~50 dBZ ring interpreted as a debris ball. A survey of 31 damage indicators documented a ~2.9 km long and up to ~340 m wide path rated IF2 on the International Fujita Scale. Processor smoothing of the radial velocity and a $\rho_{HV}$ threshold for rainfall estimation masked any tornadic vortex or debris signature, although a radial velocity simulation shows that a narrow vortex (core radius ~50-100 m) with a rotational velocity of ~35-45 m s$^{-1}$ could have been concealed. This case shows that significant tornadoes can develop at night during the Philippine monsoon season and that operational radar quality control should be revised to retain severe-storm signatures.

papers.title: Passable for Whom? Few-Shot Learning for Personal Calibration of Sidewalk Accessibility Perception for Human-Centered Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Whether a sidewalk is passable depends on who is trying to pass: people who use the same mobility aid disagree about the same image, so one label per scene, or per aid, is wrong for many of them. We introduce few-shot personal accessibility perception: from K answers of a person never seen before, predict their judgment of sidewalk scenes never seen before. PassCal separates a shared description of the scene from the person's interpretation of it. The description comes from the internal state of a frozen vision-language model (VLM) and from barrier type, severity and context properties predicted by a detector trained on 14.9k public audits; the interpretation, a calibration of the person's response style and a weighting of the properties, is fit from their answers. On 8,883 judgments in which each of 135 verified mobility-aid users rated the same 50 sidewalk scenes, with people and scenes both held out, eight answers lower the Brier score from 0.550 to 0.479. The same VLM prompted with those answers reaches 0.562, and the same calibration without the scene 0.521. Conformal risk control turns predictions into passable, blocked or "depends on you" statements with a bounded expected rate of wrong statements over people; at 5%, eight answers raise the share of decisive scenes from 27% to 42%. Audit-supervised properties improve all sixteen vision and VLM encoders we test and outperform attributes from a sidewalk navigation VLM.

papers.title: Pros4D: Modeling Evolving 4D Worlds in Latent Space for Dynamic Spatial Reasoning
papers.abstract: Dynamic spatial reasoning from monocular video enables vision-language models (VLMs) to understand how 3D environments evolve over time, supporting physical world understanding and embodied intelligence. Existing efforts primarily address observed-dynamics understanding, whereas agents in dynamic environments also require future-dynamics prediction beyond the observation boundary. Moreover, external geometric processing and textual descriptions can increase inference complexity or lose information when representing continuous dynamics. These limitations motivate a shared internal state that preserves observed dynamics and remains predictive beyond the input video. Accordingly, we present Pros4D, a framework for modeling evolving 4D worlds in latent space that unifies retrospective understanding of observed-dynamics with prospective reasoning for future-dynamics prediction. Specifically, Pros4D-Engine derives geometry-grounded supervision and constructs paired examples for both tasks, while Pros4D-Bench evaluates them across eight spatial task categories spanning dynamic cameras, objects, and scenes. At the model level, Pros4D compresses observed dynamics into latent observed states and autoregressively rolls them forward into latent future states. 4D Latent Alignment (4DLA) grounds these states through complementary visual-semantic and geometric supervision, while joint language supervision connects them to task reasoning. Experiments across benchmarks show consistent improvements over strong baselines in both capabilities.

papers.title: Machine interpreting competitiveness: a discourse-sensitive comparison of meaning and target-language quality in English-Chinese simultaneous interpreting
papers.abstract: Machine interpreting (MI), or AI-enabled speech translation, is increasingly visible in professional and public-facing communication, yet its performance relative to human simultaneous interpreters remains insufficiently understood. Existing studies are often limited by a single discourse mode and evaluation frameworks that are not well aligned with interpreting as a discourse-level communicative activity. The present study compares five commercial MI systems with 26 human interpreters (14 professionals, 12 advanced students) on English-to-Chinese simultaneous interpreting across planned and unplanned discourse, focusing on meaning and target-language quality. In these materials, MI performance differed sharply between the two discourse modes. In the planned formal speech, the strongest system became highly competitive on meaning, entering the upper human range, and a second system also performed strongly. In the extemporaneous interview, however, no MI system approached the stronger human tiers. Code-level analysis further shows that similar overall scores often masked different error profiles. Human interpreters were more likely to preserve the broader communicative trajectory through selective omission, restructuring, and contextual inference, whereas even the best MI systems were more vulnerable to semantic distortion, discourse-tracking failures, and context-insensitive interpretation. On target-language quality, the human advantage proved more stable than on meaning. Unintelligible or nonsensical output and disfluency carryover emerge as particularly salient weaknesses in machine performance, especially in spontaneous discourse. Overall, the findings are consistent with a discourse-sensitive account of where MI appears competitive, where it remains limited, and why these distinctions matter for interpreting practice, interpreter education, and future MI development.

papers.title: Ambiguous Examples Help, But Full Data Wins: Revisiting Dataset Cartography for Extractive Adversarial QA
papers.abstract: Dataset cartography argues that training dynamics can reveal regions of a dataset that matter differently for learning: easy-to-learn examples aid optimization, hard-to-learn examples often expose annotation problems, and ambiguous examples contribute strongly to out-of-distribution generalization. A striking implication of the original work is that a model trained on only 33% ambiguous examples can outperform full-data training on several OOD evaluations, including a QNLI reformulation of SQuAD evaluated on Adversarial SQuAD. We revisit this claim in a stricter setting: open-ended extractive question answering, where models must predict answer spans rather than classify question-sentence pairs. For each encoder family, we compute clean-source SQuAD training dynamics, train on full, random, easy-ranked, ambiguous-ranked, and hard-ranked subsets, and evaluate robustness on adversarial-only AddSent and AddOneSent rows. Ambiguous-ranked 33% subsets beat random 33% subsets on exact-match accuracy in all 14 model-evaluation cells and on F1 in 12/14 cells. However, full-data training beats ambiguous-ranked training in 12/14 exact-match cells and 12/14 F1 cells, with mean full-minus-ambiguous gains of 3.40 EM and 4.10 F1. The most thoroughly replicated ELECTRA-small panel is also the main exception to the ambiguous-over-random F1 gains. These results show that clean-source cartography remains useful for reduced-data selection, but its OOD advantage does not carry over as a general replacement for full-data training in extractive adversarial QA.

papers.title: On the multiplicity of the Laplacian eigenvalue 1 of a graph
papers.abstract: A connected graph $G$ with $n\ge 2$ vertices and $\varepsilon$ edges is called a \emph{$k$-cyclic graph} if $k=\varepsilon-n+1$. The Laplacian matrix is defined as $L(G)=D(G)-A(G)$, where $D(G)$ is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A(G)$ is the adjacency matrix of $G$. Let $m_{G}(1)$ be the multiplicity of the Laplacian eigenvalue $1$ of $G$. In this paper, we show that for fixed integers $n\ge \big\lceil\frac{3+\sqrt{8k+1}} {2}\big\rceil$ and $k\geq0$, if $G$ is a $k$-cyclic graph of order $n$, then \begin{equation*} \displaystyle m_{G}(1)\leq n-\big\lceil\frac{3+\sqrt{8k+1}} {2}\big\rceil \end{equation*} and moreover, we completely characterize all extremal graphs attained the upper bound.

papers.title: Structural latent dimension: deterministic geometry and local Fisher structure
papers.abstract: We study the structural dimension of a second-order object: the minimum latent dimension that remains necessary relative to a declared class of competing dependence. Building on minimum-rank factor analysis and low-rank-plus-sparse decomposition, we use distances to lower-dimensional classes to describe inference near structural ambiguity. General distance and tangent-cone facts yield confidence statements and local margins. For rank-zero competitors with bounded residual degree, we derive exact maximum-weight $b$-matching formulas, support-slack tangent cones and sparse-spike angles; a shared residual support across a field can produce separation absent pointwise. We give positive-semidefinite brackets, a dimension-free Gaussian likelihood expansion, an exact quotient by the tangent of a low-rank background, and a detection floor from the margin. Equal-angle configurations with different branch multiplicities motivate static and spectral detection conjectures. Joint low-rank/residual profiling and the sharp composite information boundaries remain open.

papers.title: Baryon Acoustic Oscillations from the all-sky Wen & Han cluster catalog and the 2MASS Redshift Survey
papers.abstract: Baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in the clustering of galaxies and quasars now measure distances to precision of about one percent although galaxy clusters have so far given only marginal signals. We measure the BAO scale in the correlation function of \vNclus\ galaxy clusters with spectroscopic redshifts at $0.1<z<0.7$ from the Wen and Han (2024) all-sky catalog. After reconstruction of the density field, the BAO peak has a significance of $\vsigpost\sigma$ against a model without it, and gives $\DV/\rd=\vDVpost\pm\vDVpoststat\,({\rm stat})\pm\vDVpostsys\,({\rm sys})$ at an effective redshift $z_{\rm eff}=\vzeffv$, a \vfracposttot\% distance. We find that the statistical uncertainty is \vratiostat\ times smaller than that of the best earlier cluster measurement. The distance agrees with the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 within $\vnsdesipost\sigma$ and lies $\vnsplanckpost\sigma$ below Planck. We also measure the BAO scale in the \vTNgal\ galaxies of the 2MASS Redshift Survey with a mean effective redshift (weighted by $n\,w^2$ with FKP weights), $z_{\rm eff}=\vTzeff$ For this all-sky galaxy sample we obtain $\aiso=\vTpreA^{+\vTpreAup}_{-\vTpreAlo}$ before reconstruction.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal K-Shape: Reconstructing inhomogeneous condensate profiles on the lattice
papers.abstract: Spatially modulated chiral condensates can affect the phase structure of dense QCD effective models. Understanding such order requires characterizing its real-space structure as well as detecting a modulation. Spatial two-point correlators retain the ensemble-averaged power spectrum but discard relative Fourier phases, leaving the configuration shapes undetermined in general. We propose the Spatiotemporal K-Shape method to extract representative shapes from lattice Monte Carlo ensembles without assuming a functional form. The method extends K-Shape clustering to periodic lattice fields, aligning configurations modulo translations and, optionally, a global sign or phase before extracting cluster centroids. Comparisons across clusterings assess whether one representative shape suffices. Controlled tests recover distinct profiles with identical correlators and separate mixtures of different shapes. Applied to the $(1+1)$-dimensional Gross-Neveu model with $N_f=8$, the method extracts non-sinusoidal profiles with two sign changes at two chemical potentials and separates multiple shape families at a third, where a single centroid is insufficient. Including the discrete chiral sign symmetry in the alignment can fold domain-length fluctuations into an asymmetric centroid without implying a preferred ensemble asymmetry. The method thus complements correlator diagnostics with representative real-space shapes and information on their diversity. The application to the Gross-Neveu model provides a testing ground for configuration-based studies of inhomogeneous order relevant to the QCD phase diagram.

papers.title: ReCALM: A Residual-enhanced Crowdsourced Analytic Learning Mechanism for Distributed Continual Service Construction
papers.abstract: Crowdsourcing has emerged as a promising paradigm for constructing AI services by harnessing the collective capabilities of distributed workers. As consumers' demands continually evolve, service models must acquire new knowledge while retaining previously learned information. However, due to the inherited reliance on gradients for backpropagation, existing approaches typically suffer from catastrophic forgetting during continual model updates on heterogeneous data. Recent studies have introduced analytic learning, a gradient-free paradigm that achieves invariance through recursive closed-form solutions. Nevertheless, existing analytic methods are typically constrained by single-layer linear networks, which tend to suffer from underfitting due to their inability to perform deep representation learning. To address this issue, we propose ReCALM, a Residual-enhanced Crowdsourced Analytic Learning Mechanism that achieves deep nonlinear invariance for distributed continual service construction. Inspired by the success of ResNet, we develop gradient-free residual blocks for ReCALM with closed-form solutions. To implement distributed continual training for ReCALM, we further devise a cross-recursive strategy via least squares. Both theoretical and experimental analyses verify ReCALM's dual superiority in heterogeneity invariance and deep representation. With 20 residual layers, ReCALM improves accuracy by 8.85%-9.83% over the single-layer analytic baseline, while reducing computational costs by over 94% compared with gradient-based baselines.

papers.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for Riesz capacity in all dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove the Brunn--Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity on compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $n-1<p<n$, extending the known endpoint $p=n-1$. For sets of positive capacity, equality holds if and only if they are convex and positively homothetic. The inequality remains conjectural for $n-2<p<n-1$, when $n\ge2$. Known isodiametric counterexamples rule out a general extension to negative $p$, even for convex planar sets.

papers.title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $\tau^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $\tau^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $\tau^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

papers.title: Live Noise Fingerprints for Quantum Program Analysis
papers.abstract: Quantum programs are probabilistic in nature, and noisy execution due to current imperfect hardware further complicates their analysis. In this paper, we study abstract semantics for analysing quantum programs under these conditions. We introduce noise fingerprints, compact descriptions of the observable effects of noise relative to a finite interface of input states and output measurements. We use them to define our abstract domain with respect to the concrete noise-related behaviour. We relate the concrete and abstract domains through a probabilistic Galois connection, extending the Galois-connection framework to distribution-valued interpretations.
