We study the resulting abstraction in terms of observational soundness, conciseness, efficiency, and ability to adapt to changing noise. We show that polynomial-size interfaces yield exponentially smaller fingerprints than full noise models while preserving the chosen observations, and that fingerprint distance characterises the largest observational discrepancy over the chosen interface. Further, we develop ChanShadow, which reuses noise fingerprints of commonly used short program fragments to analyse noisy execution of whole programs and provides a uniform finite-sample error bound. We construct working examples showing how fingerprints support program analysis. We evaluate fingerprint precision, representation cost, measurement requirements, and behaviour under noise drift. On a synthetic benchmark, fingerprints retain $(99 \pm 1)\%$ of the noise strength information of a full noise model. On simulated noise drift, reusing earlier measurements reduces the number of fresh measurement rounds needed to reach an error tolerance of $0.10$ by a factor of $2.3$ at $95\%$ confidence and by a factor of $27$ under the median-error criterion.

papers.title: SuperGlance: Driving at a Glance with a Vision-Language Model
papers.abstract: Autonomous driving is turning to vision-language-action models (VLAs). They answer and plan by decoding, one step at a time. Each step is another forward pass, so a plan can take over a second of GPU time. Embodied AI often pairs such a slow, reasoning System 2 with a fast System 1 that acts. Human drivers plan at a glance, with System 1. Faster designs usually put System 1 outside the vision-language model (VLM), in a planner without its abilities. Yet before a VLM writes its first token, it has already read the scene into one hidden state. We show that, once trained, this hidden state is enough to drive and to answer questions about what the model sees. SuperGlance reads it to turn a decoder-only VLM into an encoder-style driving policy. Its linear head scores a fixed set of 5,273 candidate trajectories. With the set fixed, rewards are computed offline, so supervised targets can be reward-weighted and reinforcement learning maximizes the exact expected reward. Before and during policy training, multiple-choice training keeps the VLM's visual abilities in one pass, so the policy still answers questions about driving scenes. Training questions are built against shortcuts. Each must be answered right in two option orders. Against drift, a KL term keeps each stage near its starting model. One pass offers VLAs a more plausible path to System 1. SuperGlance answers visual multiple-choice questions as well as its base VLM does by decoding. It plans in 84 ms of GPU time, six times faster than Qwen-Drive-1.0, and at least as well on NAVSIM, PAI-AV and WOD-E2E. In AlpaSim closed loop, km per at-fault incident holds for both planners up to a 300-ms delay and drops beyond. With GPU time charged as delay, SuperGlance's lead over Qwen-Drive-1.0 grows from 2.8 to 3.9 times. Delayed by 1.2 s, our model falls below Qwen-Drive-1.0 at its own 518 ms.

papers.title: Composable Rewrites for Layouts of Algebraic Data Types
papers.abstract: Algebraic data types (ADTs) decouple the logical structure of data from physical layout choices that affect performance. For example, packing small fields into a word improves spatial locality, while storing co-accessed fields contiguously can enable vectorization. Such choices reinforce or undermine one another, with ramifications for compiler optimizations and memory management. Their interplay creates a combinatorial space of layouts with different runtime costs and memory footprints. The most favorable layout depends on the program's construction and destruction patterns, the characteristics of input data, and the target machine. Exploring this space requires control over layout decisions and a way to compose them while preserving program semantics. We provide both through rewrite rules over layouts, independent of any particular source language or bit-level encoding. Starting from a canonical layout derived from the ADT, these rules transform its representation while leaving the source program intact. We identify a local refinement criterion for proving each rewrite rule correct, so that layouts continue to represent every value and keep distinct values apart. Adding a new rule therefore only requires a proof satisfying this local criterion. We realize these rules in Isomer, a new pure functional programming language whose compiler specializes construction, pattern matching, and memory management to the chosen layouts. Using a default layout for all ADTs, Isomer achieves competitive performance against established functional compilers that automatically select layouts. Our rewrites further improve performance by tailoring layouts to each workload, permitting representations that prior work cannot attain or can only achieve through explicit changes to the source code.

papers.title: Run, Read Back, Refine: Observation Fidelity in Execution-Grounded EDA Agents
papers.abstract: Design engineers lose the most time orchestrating flows and patching the gaps where closed EDA tools refuse to interoperate. We present an execution-grounded LLM agent for PyAether, SKILL, and Tcl that closes a generate-execute-refine loop over unified MCP tools (API retrieval, documentation, sandbox execution) and is already deployed in production EDA flows, with a grounding-gap framework positing that EDA-scripting correctness is bottlenecked by observation fidelity at the L4 (situated) layer, which model scale alone cannot reach. On EDA-Scripting-Bench (449 tasks, three languages, four commercial runtimes), the system reaches 76.5% pooled Pass@1 versus 19.7% (pure LLM): the system-level observation axis spans 56.8 percentage points with the model fixed, exceeding the 23.3-percentage-point backbone range with the harness fixed---two axes answering different questions; observation is an under-invested axis whose returns are measurable and graded.

papers.title: Lie Group Structure of Six-Degree-of-Freedom Rigid-Body Uncertainty Representation and Propagation
papers.abstract: For six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body motion, the choice of Lie-group structure affects both how well the group-theoretic mean and covariance represent the state distribution and how accurately these moments are propagated. A quaternion-based, left-trivialized semidirect-product formulation of the velocity phase space is developed for the actuated body-frame dynamics, with closed-form group operations and Jacobians that avoid matrix-group embeddings. We derive the controlled stochastic dynamics and establish that the direct- and semidirect-product formulations describe the same physical process under the specified noise model. Since the semidirect exponential coordinates account for frame changes between body twists at different poses, they capture pose--twist coupling more naturally. A lunar powered-descent experiment assesses low-order moment representations of uncertainty and propagation performance under the proposed group structure using two distinct algorithms. Compared with direct-product formulations and a linearized baseline, the proposed structure improves the representation of the banana-shaped body-velocity distribution using group-theoretic moments, yields more consistent propagated moments, and produces distribution approximations that agree more closely with the Monte Carlo reference. In this experiment, changing the group structure accounts for most of the observed improvement, highlighting the practical value of the proposed semidirect-product formulation.

papers.title: Gate tunable spin splitting for Andreev spin qubits in Ge quantum well heterostructures
papers.abstract: Ge-based super-semi heterostructures are a promising platform for implementing Andreev spin qubits (ASQs). For example, they can be isotopically purified to eliminate nuclear spins that cause decoherence. However, spin-orbit coupling (SOC), which is a key ingredient for ASQs, is cubic in momentum for hole-based materials like Ge, in contrast with more-conventional ASQ materials (e.g., InAs wires), for which the SOC is linear in momentum. In this work, we study the interplay between geometrical properties like the channel width, and gate-tunable properties like the chemical potential, on ASQ operations. Intriguingly, we find that the spin splitting in a planar Ge Josephson junction does not depend on the junction width, in contrast with InAs nanowires. We explore the possibility of exploiting this property to suppress the harmful effects of charge traps. However, this prospect is spoiled by the fact that charge traps also affect the chemical potential, in addition to the channel width. Our results provide insights into the fundamental mechanisms governing spin splitting in ASQs and offer guidance for optimizing ASQs in other materials with cubic SOC.

papers.title: Probing the QCD Conformal Window with Four-Quark Operators
papers.abstract: The infrared fate of QCD-like theories and their conformal window for different numbers or flavours and colour remains an open question with applications ranging from high-energy to condensed-matter systems. A hallmark of phase transitions from a conformal to symmetry breaking phase can be the presence of classically irrelevant operators that provide relevant deformation in the infrared. We investigate this scenario by computing anomalous dimensions of all four-quark operators, with or without chiral symmetry, at four-loop order as well as the dimension-six gluonic operator at three loops in Veneziano QCD. Scaling dimensions are derived in a systematic conformal expansion. These results are improved with various resummation techniques and we estimate their uncertainties. We find no concrete evidence for a composite operator effectively describing a merger with the QCD fixed point.

papers.title: The effect of policy cancellation on the risk of an insurance portfolio
papers.abstract: For an insurance portfolio modelled by a large number of i.i.d. losses, the average loss converges to its expected value by the law of large numbers, reflecting the diversification effect of pooling risks. Policy cancellations reduce the portfolio size and thereby weaken this effect. We quantify the resulting increase in risk by applying risk measures to the average loss before and after the cancellation of policies. For a portfolio of size $n$, we show that the impact of cancelling a single contract is of order $n^{-3/2}$, while the cancellation of a fixed proportion of contracts has an effect of order $n^{-1/2}$. We further extend the proportional cancellation regime to heterogeneous portfolios with different cancellation rates and risk characteristics across segments. These asymptotic results provide a quantitative basis for assessing surrender fees and cancellation costs from the insurer's perspective. We complement the theoretical analysis with numerical results for representative life insurance products, illustrating the magnitude of cancellation costs and the effect of portfolio aggregation. The two regimes require different techniques. For the cancellation of a fixed proportion of contracts, we employ central limit theorems in Wasserstein distance. For the cancellation of a single contract, we combine Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality with higher-order distributional approximations based on the Edgeworth and Cornish-Fisher expansions.

papers.title: FlashREINFORCE: Critic-Free Single-Rollout Asynchronous RL for Agentic Language Models
papers.abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning suits long-horizon agents with irregular rollout times, but group-relative updates require repeated rollouts of each prompt. However, group-based sampling limits prompt coverage at a fixed rollout budget and introduces group synchronization barriers. One rollout per prompt avoids these constraints but requires learning from stale, variable-length trajectories without a sibling baseline. We present FlashREINFORCE, to our knowledge the first critic-free single-rollout framework that scales to long asynchronous training and large models. It combines One-Batch REINFORCE, a Sequence Trust Region, and Sample-Mean Optimization, which provide prompt coverage and batch centering while controlling policy drift and length-amplified negative updates. Each component is easy to implement, and the result is their combination: a batch-mean baseline is stable under sample-mean loss, and each common alternative degrades or collapses training. FlashREINFORCE remains stable through 6,000 updates on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B at policy lag four, and through 1,450 on the 30B MoE Qwen3-30B-A3B at lag eight. Under identical loss, data, and lag it matches a strengthened group-relative baseline within 0.5 points, and with half the rollouts exceeds published synchronous baselines on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B (38.0 versus 36.3 five-benchmark mean). On Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct it maintains tool use where GRPO stops calling tools and achieves 98.3%/96.5% seen/unseen ALFWorld success.

papers.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
papers.abstract: We introduce Gamer, a generalist agent framework built for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive environments. Its end-to-end architecture combines perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning. A shared training and deployment pipeline supports interaction with both conventional 2D graphical interfaces and complex 3D simulated worlds. We first continue pre-training on a dataset constructed from tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction. These trajectories span simulated games and embodied environments, allowing the model to learn environmental dynamics across both physical and virtual domains. Sparse-thinking instruction tuning then substantially reduces redundant computation while preserving the reasoning needed for complex decisions. We train the policy for long-horizon interaction with a stable multi-turn reinforcement learning method that addresses finite context windows, accumulated rollout errors, and sparse rewards. For real-time interaction, a cloud-edge inference engine serves numerous simulated game environments concurrently, supports unbounded-context execution, and keeps online inference latency low. Across multiple challenging 3D open-world games, Gamer demonstrates solid generalization and operational efficiency comparable to skilled players. It also achieves competitive results on a range of conventional 2D game benchmarks. These results suggest that even repetitive keyboard and mouse trajectories can support substantial gains from scaling data and learning algorithms. Training on these trajectories helps Gamer learn complex skills more steadily in environments with both physical and digital properties. This approach offers a path toward generalist agents that can interact across digital and physical worlds.

papers.title: The Capillary Dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
papers.abstract:
We study a capillary dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski problem on a spherical cap. For $2\le k\le n$, $1<p<k+1$, and $0<	heta<\pi/2$, we consider \[ \sigma_k(
abla^2h+h\sigma) = f(\xi)h^{p-1} rac{ho^{k+1}}{\varphi(ho)}, \qquad ho=(h^2+|
abla h|^2)^{1/2}, \] with the capillary Robin condition $
abla_\mu h=\cot	heta\,h$. Assuming that $f$ is positive, smooth and horizontally even, $g=f^{-1/(p+k-1)}$ satisfies the capillary spherical-convexity and boundary compatibility conditions, and $H(r)=\varphi(r)/r^p$ is strictly increasing and proper with $Q_\varphi(r)\le k+1$, we prove the existence of a smooth, positive, horizontally even solution that is strictly capillary convex. The proof uses an Orlicz homotopy, uniform a priori estimates, a viscosity constant-rank argument when $k<n$, global oblique regularity, and degree theory.

papers.title: TetraCoder: Adaptive Tetrahedral Encoding for Neural Fields
papers.abstract: Implicit and explicit representations of geometry are central in computer graphics applications and come with their pros and cons. With surface sampling being faster on explicit representations and spatial queries being faster on implicit representations, finding efficient conversions between them is a highly desirable property. We present TetraCoder, a single resolution hash-free adaptive tetrahedral encoding that links an explicit tetrahedral spatial encoder with an underlying implicit signed distance field (SDF). The resulting hybrid implicit-explicit space is continuous piecewise affine (CPWA) by design, allowing to obtain an exact correspondence between the implicit SDF and the explicit analytic mesh. TetraCoder's design comes with additional perks, in particular: (a) it scales better than multi-resolution encoding methods due to its single resolution optimizable grid, (b) unlike hash-based methods, it is not affected by collisions, (c) it enables fast tetrahedral ray-tracing, geometry and appearance editing, directly through its adaptive tetrahedral scaffold. We demonstrate the versatility of TetraCoder by showing an improvement over state-of-the-art methods on multiple tasks: 2D/3D fitting from images and point clouds, 3D novel view synthesis, 3D reconstruction, and geometry/appearance editing.

papers.title: Short quadratic exponential sums with primes in major arcs
papers.abstract: Using the second moment of Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line over the major arcs ${\mathfrak M}({\mathscr L}^b)$, with $\tau=y^3x^{-1}{\mathscr L}^{-b_1}$, and excluding a small neighborhood of the centers of these arcs, i.e., those $\alpha$ satisfying $|\alpha-\frac{a}{q}|>(8\pi y^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{1-\frac{\scriptstyle1}{\scriptstyle{9-4\sqrt{2}}}}{\mathscr L}^{c_2}$, where $c_2=\frac{2A+24+(\sqrt{2}-1)b_1}{2\sqrt{2}-1}$, we obtain the estimate $$ S_2(\alpha;x,y)=\sum_{x-y<n\le x}\Lambda(n)e(\alpha n^2)\ll y\,{\mathscr L}^{-A}. $$ Moreover, in a small neighborhood of the center of the major arcs, defined by $|\alpha-\frac{a}{q}|\le(8\pi y^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{\frac{\scriptstyle5}{\scriptstyle8}}{\mathscr L}^{1,5A+0,25b+18}$, an asymptotic formula with a remainder term is obtained for $S_2(\alpha;x,y)$, where $A$, $b_1$, and $b$ are arbitrary fixed positive constants, and ${\mathscr L}=\ln xq$.

papers.title: Explanations that Transfer: Interpreting Medical Retrieval with Sparse AutoEncoders
papers.abstract: Medical AI systems that answer users' queries rely on retrieving medical knowledge from large document collections. In this context, finetuning general models on medical datasets can improve retrieval relevance. Yet the dense embeddings underlying modern retrieval systems remain largely opaque, making it difficult to understand the mechanics behind their results. Moreover, adapting to a specific medical dataset risks losing transferability to new clinical corpora. In this work, we tackle these issues by applying Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to medical information retrieval, transforming dense text embeddings into semantically interpretable representations. To do so, our model combines a reconstruction objective with an InfoNCE contrastive loss that directly preserves query-document relevance. We evaluate three embedding models across six medical retrieval datasets, both in-domain and out-of-domain. Trained on a medical corpus, our sparse codes improve in-domain retrieval over the original embeddings, and lose less out-of-domain performance than their dense counterparts, especially when the target corpus is distant from the training one. Importantly, our experiments show that the method yields interpretable features whose semantic content can be inferred from the queries and documents that activate them most strongly. The interpretation of these features sheds light on why a particular document was retrieved, and transfers beyond the training distribution.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) : Performance of the redshift measurement and spectroscopic analysis
papers.abstract: The European Space Agency's Euclid mission has issued its first major data release(Data Release 1, DR1), providing a transformative view of the extragalactic sky through deep photometry and near-infrared slitless spectroscopy. This paper presents the Euclid DR1 spectroscopic data set and details the evolution of the spectroscopic processing function (SPE PF) pipeline, which is responsible for the automated analysis of 1-dimensional spectra acquired by the Near-Infrared Spectro-Photometer (NISP). The SPE PF pipeline workflow comprises spectroscopic classification, redshift determination, and the systematic measurement of spectral features. Emission line fluxes are derived using two independent methodologies: direct integration (DI) and Gaussian fitting (GF). For sources exhibiting broad H$\alpha$ profiles (velocity dispersion larger than $1500$ km s$^{-1}$), a dedicated `QSO mode' is implemented to robustly deconvolve nuclear and host galaxy components. The data set was validated by cross-matching Euclid results with external spectroscopic catalogues, specifically Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR1, and through an extensive visual inspection campaign of approximately 4000 sources within the Euclid Deep Field North (EDF-N). For high-quality samples selected in the EDF-N, we find a 98.5\% agreement between Euclid and DESI spectroscopic redshifts. This success rate increases to 98.9\% when incorporating pipeline probability and reliability estimators. (abridged)

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): The MERge processing
papers.abstract: The ESA satellite mission \Euclid was launched in July 2023 and started its regular observing mode in February 2024. The data from the \Euclid instruments Visible Camera (VIS) and the Near IR Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) are complemented by ground-based imaging data in the $u$, $g$ $r$, $i$, and $z$ bands to enable the determination of photometric redshifts and other galaxy properties. This paper describes the MERge processing function (MER PF) that has been developed and run for the Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). The aim of the MER PF is to detect objects in the \Euclid imaging data, measure their properties, and combine them into a single multi-wavelength catalogue. In this paper we illustrate the design of the MER PF and introduce the different photometric methods applied to the data, which are Kron total flux, aperture photometry on Point Spread Functions (PSF) -matched images, template fitting photometry, and S\'ersic fitting photometry. We also present the various morphological measurements and quality flags that improve the scientific content of the output catalogues and better characterize the detected sources. We illustrate the processing and measurements that help to validate the MER PF results, which is an essential step to qualify the output for the public DR1 release. We discuss the global assessment of the photometric homogeneity and provide an internal comparison of our processing results. In addition, we give an extensive overview of the DR1 output data and the various processing scenarios

papers.title: An accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose an accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping for unconstrained convex multiobjective optimization problems in a real Hilbert space. The continuous flow is formulated as a system of two first-order equations involving only a single multiobjective projection operator and suitable time-scaling factors. Formally, it can also be expressed as a second-order system with explicit multiobjective Hessian-driven damping, which corresponds to the usual Hessian-driven damping introduced by Alvarez et al. [J. Math. Pures Appl., 81(8):747--779, 2002]. The first-order formulation, however, involves no Hessian term and can be regarded as an extension of the Hessian-driven Nesterov accelerated gradient flow by Chen and Luo [arXiv:1912.09276, 2019]. Assuming that the objective gradients are Lipschitz continuous on bounded sets and that the common lower level sets are bounded, we establish global existence in finite dimensions under suitable time-scaling conditions. An a priori energy estimate confines the solutions to a fixed bounded set, and a Lyapunov argument yields fast decay of a merit function and the KKT residual. Under an additional bound on the time-scaling factors, the trajectory of every global solution converges weakly to a weak Pareto point. Numerical tests illustrate the rapid residual decay and reduced oscillations.

papers.title: Anyon Proliferation at Self-Triality: From a Lattice Model to Adjoint QCD$_3$
papers.abstract: We study how competitive proliferation among three types of anyons in a self-trial $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ gauge theory can drive symmetry breaking while preserving part of the topological order. We construct a deformation of the honeycomb color code, a spin model rooted in quantum error correction, with an $S_3$ symmetry that permutes the competing anyons, together with time-reversal and fermionic $\mathbb Z_2^{(1)}$ one-form symmetries. We propose two dual continuum descriptions of this transition. The bosonic description is a $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_3\times\mathrm{Spin}(8)_{-1}$ Chern--Simons--Higgs theory with a real Higgs field in the $(\mathbf8_{\mathrm{adj}},\mathbf8_v)$ representation. Fermion-boson duality gives a particularly simple fermionic dual: $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_{3/2}$ QCD$_3$ with a single adjoint Majorana fermion and gauged fermion parity. Both descriptions match the lattice model's symmetries and proposed phase diagram, connecting double-toric-code order to a symmetry-broken phase with residual toric-code order. The transition is described by Higgs condensation and by a Majorana mass changing sign, respectively. This connection to adjoint QCD$_3$ points to a possible continuous $S_3$-breaking transition from competing anyons, in contrast to the conventional first-order three-state Potts transition from competing local order parameters.

papers.title: Simulating Space Bounded Read-$k$ PTMs with Space Bounded Read-Once PTMs
papers.abstract: We show that read-$k$ Probabilistic Turing Machines with bounded space $S$ and running time $T$ can be simulated by read-once Probabilistic Turing Machines with error $\varepsilon$, running in space $ O(k^2 (S + \log (n+ T)) + \log (1/\epsilon))$ and time $\frac{1}{\varepsilon} \cdot 2^{O\left(k^2\left(S+\log(n+T) \right)\right)}$. As a direct consequence we show that read-$k$ $\mathsf{BPL}$ is equal to $\mathsf{BPL}$, for any constant $k$. Recently OpenAI announced that $\mathsf{BPL} = \mathsf{L}$. If this is true then our result immediately implies that read-$k$ $\mathsf{BPL}$ is equal to $\mathsf{L}$.

papers.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz capacity in one dimension
papers.abstract: The Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity is proved on the line for every $p<1$ and all compact sets. For $-1<p<1$, equality holds exactly for a singleton summand or else two intervals, provided at least one capacity is positive. The proof couples equilibrium measures in increasing order.

papers.title: Equilibrium points of logarithmic potentials
papers.abstract: We construct logarithmic potentials with positive masses at a sequence of points tending to infinity and with no critical points. These potentials can have any prescribed order $\rho \in [1/2, 1)$; for $\rho = 1/2$ we obtain examples of both normal and maximal type. For $1/2 < \rho < 1$, the masses at conjugate poles are prescribed by a power law. We determine the pole asymptotics and the angular growth of these potentials. For sums of simple fractions with absolutely summable complex residues and nonzero sum of residues, we prove the existence of infinitely many zeros and compare their counting function with that of the poles.

papers.title: Finding the Farthest in High Dimensions: Dynamic Diameter and Farthest-Neighbor Search
papers.abstract: We give algorithms for maintaining diameter in the dynamic model, and for answering farthest-neighbor queries on a fixed point set, in high-dimensional Euclidean space. For every fixed $1<c<\sqrt2$, update horizon $t$, and error probability $\delta$, we maintain an actual factor-$c$ diameter pair with worst-case update time $n^{2/c^2-1}\text{poly}_c(d,\log(2nt/\delta))$ and space $n^{2/c^2}\text{poly}_c(d,\log(2nt/\delta))$. Here $n$ bounds the number of active point identities. The update exponent improves Indyk's SODA~2003 bound from $1/c^2$ to $2/c^2-1$, while the space exponent improves from $1+1/c^2$ to $2/c^2$. At $c=\sqrt{3/2}$, the update exponent decreases from $2/3$ to $1/3$. A separate construction achieves approximation exactly $\sqrt2$ with update time polynomial in $d$ and $\log(2nt/\delta)$. With probability at least $1-\delta$, every maintained answer during the first $t$ updates is correct, even when updates depend on all previous answers and random choices. A second construction improves the update exponent when the space exponent is close to one. On rational inputs, it has an always-correct variant with expected amortized update bounds over every fixed finite prefix of an adaptive execution, without an advance update horizon. The dynamic structures store a current answer, so reporting its two point identifiers takes constant time. The geometric method also gives static diameter algorithms and a farthest-neighbor structure for a fixed set that answers arbitrary adaptive queries. At approximation $\sqrt2-\varepsilon$, the diameter time is $n^{1+O(\varepsilon)}$, and the query time is $n^{O(\varepsilon)+o(1)}$ with near-linear preprocessing and space, up to polynomial input-parameter factors.

papers.title: Symmetry-preserving gapped Dirac state revealed by site-selective $^{13}$C NMR in $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$
papers.abstract: We report evidence that the low-temperature insulating phase of $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$ preserves both inversion and time-reversal symmetries using site-selective $^{13}$C nuclear magnetic resonance. $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$ undergoes a metal-insulator transition or sharp crossover at approximately 50 K and has been proposed as a candidate spin-orbit-coupling-induced Dirac insulator, yet the nature of its insulating ground state remains unresolved. The NMR spectra exhibit no additional splitting down to 2 K and remain fully described by one quartet and two doublets associated with the three types of molecular sites, A (=A$^{\prime}$), B and C sites, demonstrating the preservation of inversion symmetry. Furthermore, no anomalous line broadening or critical enhancement of the nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate is observed, indicating the absence of magnetic ordering and time-reversal-symmetry breaking. Analysis of the Knight shifts yields site-specific spin susceptibilities satisfying $\chi_{\mathrm{C}} > \chi_{\mathrm{A}} > \chi_{\mathrm{B}}$, a characteristic feature of tilted Dirac-cone electronic states as observed in $\alpha$-(BEDT-TTF)$_2$I$_3$ under pressure. However, the faint field-induced ferrimagnetic-like spin excitations observed in $\alpha$-(BEDT-TTF)$_2$I$_3$, which are ascribed to the gapless tilted Dirac cones, are absent in $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$. These results demonstrate that the insulating ground state of $\alpha$-(BETS)$_2$I$_3$ is a symmetry-preserving gapped Dirac state and provide microscopic constraints on proposed correlated topological phases in this molecular Dirac system.

papers.title: Margin-Inducing Optimal Guidance and Control for Atmospheric Entry
papers.abstract: A method is presented for margin-inducing optimal guidance and control with application to atmospheric entry. The method induces margin in state inequality path constraints during entry while simultaneously retaining a large portion of the non-margin-inducing performance. The margin in the guidance trajectory is based on a differentiable approximation of the maximum of a continuous function. This differentiable approximation is derived from the Kreisselmeier-Steinhauser (KS) function, where the KS function is defined for a function over sampled data. The KS function is first modified into a weighted form where the data points and weights are associated with a multiple-interval Legendre-Gauss-Radau quadrature. This weighted form is then shown to be an approximation of a logarithmic integral. This smooth approximation of the maximum function is then used to formulate a margin-inducing optimal control problem, and this margin-inducing optimal control problem is re-solved at specified guidance update times. The method is applied to a reusable launch vehicle atmospheric entry problem subject to heating rate and dynamic pressure constraints. It is found that the method of this paper produces a guidance trajectory that remains a significant distance from the path constraint limits while maintaining a large portion of the performance of the constrained optimal control problem.

papers.title: Dynamic Scenario-Based Portfolio Optimization for Multi-Asset ETFs
papers.abstract: Portfolio outcomes may depend as much on trading restrictions as on how returns are modeled. We compared historical moving-window returns with conditional scenarios from ARMA--GARCH models and a Student-$t$ copula for 30 U.S.-listed exchange-traded funds. Matched mean--variance and conditional value-at-risk portfolios were evaluated under long-only and limited long--short bounds over 946 sessions. Historical portfolios had higher observed reward--risk ratios in most comparisons, but no paired difference remained significant after multiple-testing adjustment. Conditional scenarios did not consistently reduce realized downside risk. We distinguished changes in target weights from trades required to rebalance holdings after market movements. Relaxing the target-adjustment limit changed exposures, turnover, and some returns more than varying scenario count or seed in the examined tests. These findings suggest that assessments of conditional return inputs should consider portfolio constraints and trading requirements.

papers.title: Scale-rich network metamaterials grow by local rules on a recursive cell division
papers.abstract: Scale-rich (SR) metamaterials are planar ligament networks grown by nucleating a segment at a random point and angle and extending it until it meets the existing structure. In the dual graph, where ligaments are nodes and junctions are links, the degree distribution has a $k^{-3}$ tail that was attributed to a spatial preferential attachment. We show that the SR dual belongs to the class of local growth rules. The construction is Cowan's iterated cell division; as a graph, each new node joins two nodes on the boundary of one face. The degree distribution follows from a rate equation whose attachment kernel $(a+bk)/t$ is deduced from this local sampling. A ligament of degree $k$ borders $k$ cells, and a random point reaches it through them, so $b=2/\langle n\rangle=1/2$ with $\langle n\rangle=4$ sides per cell, and a sum rule gives $a=0$. The rate equation then gives $p_k=12/[k(k+1)(k+2)]$ with no free parameter. The measured kernel and degree distribution agree with this prediction. Preferential attachment is thus the mean-field outcome of local sampling, not a mechanism. Ligaments are hit in proportion to their length, which is fixed at birth, so the effective attachment carries no reinforcement. The same face-local step produces the signature of the local class. The probability that a new ligament cuts off a corner of its cell sets the triangle closure and the hierarchical clustering spectrum $C(k)\simeq2p/k$, and square-closing splits raise the shortest-path multiplicity above its value at fixed degree sequence. Thickness, jamming, angle sets and density gradients leave $\gamma=3$; coherent orientation fields give $\gamma\simeq2.4$--$2.5$. In $d$ dimensions the cell hierarchy fixes $b=(d-1)/d$, so plates in three dimensions have $b=2/3$ and $\gamma=5/2$, as measured. The reported per-ligament energy law cannot distinguish degree from length or age.

papers.title: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) - First NISP emission-line maps: Methodology, validation, and applications to galaxy evolution
papers.abstract: We demonstrate the capability of the slitless spectroscopic mode of the Euclid Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) to produce emission-line maps analogous to narrow-band images with user-defined central wavelengths. We present the first such maps of galaxies at $0.4 < z < 0.9$, constructed from blue-grism exposures obtained during the Euclid performance-verification observations of the Cosmic Evolution Survey (COSMOS) field in November 2023. We demonstrate the use of these maps for identifying star-forming clumps, measuring radial star-formation profiles, detecting projected internal velocity gradients, deblending the H$\alpha$--[N II] complex, and assessing spectroscopic redshift measurements. As a first statistical application, we reconstruct the galaxy mass--metallicity relation for 885 galaxies observed with the blue grism at $0.4 < z < 0.9$ by deblending the H$\alpha$--[N II] complex in the emission-line maps, and measure stacked H$\alpha$ radial profiles for 2634 galaxies over the same redshift range. The mass--metallicity relation is consistent with that obtained from the Euclid 1D spectroscopic measurements, demonstrating overall agreement between the two deblending approaches. The recovered H$\alpha$ radial profiles broadly follow the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ stellar continuum but remain modestly more extended after matching the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ images to the H$\alpha$ PSF, consistent with previous results in the literature. Across the four $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ size bins, we measure a mean $R_{50,\mathrm{H}\alpha}/R_{50,Y_{\mathrm{E}}}=1.15$.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). NIR astrometric calibration
papers.abstract: This paper presents the methodology and results of the astrometric calibration applied to the Euclid Near-Infrared (NIR) images in the Euclid Data Release 1, focusing on the techniques used to model and correct instrumental distortions, as well as the assessment of calibration quality. This work details the calibration pipeline, including quality control tests, and the evaluation of astrometric residuals against the Gaia DR3 catalogue and internal consistency metrics based on data encompassing more than one year of Euclid operation: the achieved accuracy is 30 mas for 97% of the total area, thus exceeding the requirements for Data Release 1. For the remaining 3%, accuracy declines due to a persistence correction issue: a method to correct the issue is presented. Furthermore, we discuss the stability of the solution over time, its dependence on source properties and instrument configuration, and outline the improvements planned for future Euclid data releases to enhance the astrometric calibration accuracy and efficiency.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). The PHZ processing function for the physical properties of galaxies
papers.abstract: Euclid is a European Space Agency mission mapping the extragalactic sky, aiming to provide the most-accurate 3D view of the Universe at optical and near-infrared wavelengths, by measuring the photometric redshifts of billions of galaxies. Within the Euclid Consortium, this task is executed by the PHZ Organisation Unit. PHZ takes as input the multi-wavelength photometry of Euclid and ground-based data, and returns as output the source classification, photometric redshifts for the Euclid core science (i.e., cosmology), and photometric redshifts plus physical parameters and absolute magnitudes for non-cosmological science. As part of the first Euclid Data Release (DR1), we describe the details of the DR1 pipeline for non-cosmological science, along with the released data products, and their validation. The non-cosmological science data products are obtained with NNPZ, a nearest-neighbour algorithm developed within PHZ that infers the properties of each target galaxy from its closest matches, in colour-magnitude space, within a reference sample of galaxies with known redshifts and physical parameters. We built this reference sample from Euclid observations of COSMOS, one of the Euclid Auxiliary Fields, labelling each galaxy with redshifts and physical parameters derived from the COSMOS2020 multi-wavelength photometry, consistently with the Euclid core-science results. Combined with the adjustments and priors required to generalise the results across the entire extragalactic sky, this approach yields high-quality and internally consistent data products. We tested the performance using both internal metrics and comparisons to ancillary data sets (e.g., COSMOS2020, 3D-HST, and DESI) and scaling relations (e.g., the star-forming main sequence); the results are in line with expectations and pre-DR1 simulations for both the Euclid Wide Survey and Euclid Deep Fields.

papers.title: Local Coordination for Efficient Small-Model RL on TPUs
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) increasingly targets small language models, and executing these workloads efficiently across multiple accelerators requires effective coordination. On TPUs, Pathways-based RL uses a single controller to coordinate computation across hosts. This execution model is effective for large models, but its coordination computational costs are harder to amortize when small models repeatedly invoke short computations. To characterize these computational costs, we sweep dense models from 0.6B to 405B parameters on TPU v7x under a decode-heavy workload and measure how host and network computational overhead vary with model size. At 0.6B, host orchestration occupies 36% of step time and network communication 2%, whereas for large models, estimated network computational costs dominate the non-compute time. Motivated by these findings, we present Local Coordination JAX (LoCoJAX), which implements local rollout and reward processing on each TPU host with synchronous global training. In controlled comparisons against a tuned and optimized Pathways baseline on Qwen3-0.6B across three workloads and 8-64 TPU v7x chips, its colocated mode (LoCoJAX-CO) is 1.3-3.6x faster per step; on GSM8K, it completes a step faster on 8 chips than Pathways does on 64. Finally, a Ray-managed disaggregated mode (LoCoJAX-DA) overlaps rollout and training on separate hosts, and placement experiments establish when this overlap compensates for dividing devices and transferring weights: only when rollout dominates the step and receives most of the hosts. On NuminaMath-CoT at 256 chips, giving rollout 75% of hosts cuts step time by about 15% compared with LoCoJAX-CO.

papers.title: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) -- Bayesian 3D shape inference of star-forming galaxy populations
papers.abstract: Understanding the intrinsic 3D shapes of galaxies provides crucial insights into their formation and evolution, but determining these from projections remains challenging. We apply a Bayesian inference framework to optical images of galaxies from the Euclid Data Release 1, leveraging its large sample size to test the scalability and robustness of this methodology. Applying Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling to S\'ersic axis ratios and effective radii, we constrain the population-level mean 3D ellipticity, triaxiality, and size, together with their covariances for $40\,864\,304$ star-forming galaxies with stellar masses $M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{10.5}M_\odot$ at redshifts $0<z<1.2$. Our sample size exceeds previous shape inference studies by factors of $440$--$52\,800$ relative to early observations by JWST, and factors of $440$--$17\,600$ relative to legacy observations from HST in overlapping mass-redshift bins, enabling finer binning alongside improved statistical constraints on shape evolution. We additionally include over 9 million galaxies at $z<0.5$, a regime historically limited by sample size in previous shape inference studies. We recover key evolutionary trends identified in previous smaller-sample studies. We find high ellipticities ($\mu_E \sim 0.600$--$0.821$) across all bins, indicating that the underlying 3D shape distributions are statistically dominated by flattened geometries. Most notably, we recover the decline of the prolate fraction towards $z=0$ at low masses ($M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{9.5}M_\odot$) reported by previous studies. This trend is seen consistently in comparable analyses of independent data sets spanning different depths and resolution regimes, showing that it is not an artefact of small-sample statistics, suggesting it may be a genuine feature of galaxy evolution. We also identify future methodological improvements for subsequent Euclid data releases.

papers.title: A Matching Lower Bound for Online Smooth Calibration
papers.abstract: We study smooth calibration error in sequential binary prediction, a measure of how far probabilistic forecasts are from being calibrated that is robust to small perturbations of the forecasts. The minimax smooth calibration error is known to lie between $\Omega(T^{1/3})$ and $O(\sqrt T)$(Qiao and Zheng, 2024), where $T$ is the number of rounds. We close this gap for both adaptive and oblivious adversaries. We construct an adaptive adversary whose outcome mean moves with the forecaster's cumulative residual, which makes compensating for past residuals costly and forces every forecaster to incur $\Omega(\sqrt T)$ expected smooth calibration error. Simulating this adversary against the forecaster's average prediction yields an oblivious adversary with the same guarantee. These lower bounds match the known $O(\sqrt T)$ upper bound up to universal constants, and are therefore minimax optimal. Our results also imply matching $\Theta(\sqrt T)$ bounds for calibration distance and lower calibration distance. The proof ideas are partially developed by GPT-6 Astra under the authors' guidance.

papers.title: Strangeness in the Chiral Mean Field model phase diagram
papers.abstract: We explore the phase diagram of the Chiral Mean Field model in the space of temperature and baryon, charge, and strangeness chemical potentials, focusing on the role of the strangeness direction. At low density, a negative $\mu_S$ leads to finite strangeness in the nuclear liquid--gas transition and rotates the order parameter away from the purely baryonic direction. The critical mode remains baryon dominated over the $\mu_S$ range considered, while the critical locus develops a strong parametrization dependence once multistrange baryons appear. At higher density, a separate first-order transition toward strangeness-rich hadronic matter appears only for one of the two parametrizations considered, emphasizing its interaction dependence. The high density transition reorganizes octet-dominated matter into decuplet-dominated matter: $\Delta$ baryons provide most of the baryon-density discontinuity, while $\Xi^*(1530)$ baryons provide the largest contribution to the strangeness-density discontinuity. Its order parameter is dominated by the strangeness density, and its normalized direction in the $BQS$ space changes little with temperature even as the discontinuity vanishes at the critical point. The critical baryon chemical potential changes by almost $1$~GeV over $\mu_S\in [-300, 300]$~MeV. We characterize both transitions using the fixed-temperature $BQS$ susceptibility matrix, the density discontinuity between the coexisting phases, and a generalized Clausius--Clapeyron relation. This work also accompanies the release of \cmfpp{} \texttt{v2.0.0} as part of the MUSES framework. The extension of the initial release includes, among other features, finite-temperature thermodynamics, new interactions and parametrizations, and susceptibility calculations based on a Jacobian method.

papers.title: VibePrevisBench: Evaluating Agentic Coding for 4D Scene Generation in Blender
papers.abstract: Controllable real-world video generation models can condition on a rendered graybox proxy video, which fixes layout, motion and camera. Coding agents can build such videos by generating a 4D scene in Blender, yet no benchmark checks both these rendered proxy videos and the complex, multi-shot scenes behind them. We introduce VibePrevisBench, a benchmark for 4D scene generation: an agent turns a brief into an executable 4D scene and renders its proxy video. Its 242 tasks span four input kinds, including scripts, photos, continuations, and reference videos. Each delivery is scored along two evaluation dimensions. Rule-based Scene Check re-runs the code and compares the exported 4D scene with hidden ground truth facts in nine dimensions. VLM-based Screen Check asks a VLM judge whether facts that pass the rules are recognizable in the proxy video. We analyze the evaluation results and trajectories of 11 frontier coding agents and identify three key observations. First, multimodal understanding separates the agents, especially in understanding space and camera motion. Second, all agents seem to already master basic camera work and staging, and fail at challenging requests. Third, agents inspect their own renders but fail to correct their errors. Agents thus need better visual understanding of space and camera, explicit checks for challenging requests, and item-by-item verification of renders against the brief.

papers.title: Symmetry-Enabled Ferroelectric Valley Transduction in Rhombohedral Bilayer WSe$_2$
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric polarization couples to the layer degree of freedom in a bilayer, but a valley-selective energy response requires the valleys to carry different interlayer character. Rhombohedral bilayer WSe$_2$ meets that condition by symmetry: three-fold rotation forbids interlayer tunneling at the $K$ valley, while strong hybridization remains at $\Gamma$. The resulting contrast converts the band-effective ferroelectric layer asymmetry into a shift of the $K$ edge, and so displaces the $K$--$\Gamma$ landscape: a finite-field fit that does not impose the rule leaves the $K$ coupling consistent with zero, and the shift reaches 41.7 meV, the most that asymmetry can give a single valley. Reversing the polarization mirrors the valley landscape in displacement field, so the two registries have equal and opposite differential transconductance $g_d$ at zero field. In the ideal symmetric limit a second parity holds about each registry's own compensation field and places a zero of $g_d$ there. The valley-dependent screening calculated here displaces that zero by only 0.2 % at the read point, so device asymmetry limits the accuracy. The result links a known stacking selection rule to ferroelectric valley transduction, with a quantitative valley shift and a directly testable transport signature.

papers.title: AcrossPlace: Do Vision--Language Models Recognize Places Beyond Their Source Views? A Comprehensive Benchmark
papers.abstract: Language-guided place recognition requires recovering geographic identity across visual observations beyond the image from which a description originates. However, aggregate retrieval scores often entangle observation transfer, gallery competition, and linguistic evidence, obscuring the underlying recognition capability. We introduce AcrossPlace, a provenance-aware benchmark establishing a systematic evaluation standard for bidirectional language--vision place recognition. Built upon GSV-Cities, AcrossPlace comprises 56,726 places across 23 cities, 156,800 automatically generated, rule-filtered descriptions, and 113,404 target images. Each description retains its source-image provenance, while retrieval operates on disjoint target observations. Text-to-image (T2I) and image-to-text (I2T) retrieval share a unified place-identity relevance criterion supporting multiple valid matches. Two geographic protocols evaluate unseen places within represented cities (P0) and generalization to held-out cities (P1). Paired observation comparisons, gallery-controlled evaluations, fixed-query scaling, and blinded annotation auditing systematically characterize retrieval performance. Across three training seeds, place-supervised SigLIP2 T2I Recall@1 decreases from 19.69% on source images to 12.31% on independent targets under P0. For fixed P1 queries, expanding the gallery from 500 to 8,425 places reduces Recall@1 from 14.67% to 2.87%. A 240-description audit further reveals discrepancies between automated acceptance and factual evidence. These findings establish AcrossPlace as a reproducible evaluation standard for assessing transferable place identity across visual observations and geographic environments.

papers.title: Typed Knowledge over Constructive Institutions: A Proof-Relevant Type Theory for Verified Science
papers.abstract: Mathematical proof assistants such as Coq, Agda, and Lean 4 build proof irrelevance into definitional conversion ($p \equiv q$ for $p, q : P$ with $P : Prop$), erasing which derivation established a theorem. While natural for mathematics over fixed axioms, judgmental proof irrelevance is incompatible with verified scientific stores, which must inspect and compare independent derivations of a claim to assess consilience and compute counterfactual retractions when an assay, reagent, or model is invalidated. Moreover, combining definitional proof irrelevance with subsingleton elimination breaks normalization and makes algorithmic conversion non-transitive. We present the type-theoretic and institutional foundations of Eigenius, a verified knowledge substrate for science. First, we formulate a dependent kernel with cumulative universes ($Prop, Set, Type_k$), impredicative $Prop$, inductive families with index-forced subsingleton elimination, and intensional identity types, where definitional equality $\equiv$ is untyped joinability under an orthogonal CRS and proof irrelevance is a witnessed axiom ($irrel : \Pi P{:}Prop.\,\Pi p,q{:}P.\,Id\,P\,p\,q$). Second, we unify universe cumulativity, $\Pi$-covariant subtyping, and ontology class inclusions in a coercion-free subsumption judgment whose bidirectional fragments ($\mathcal{K}_0, \mathcal{K}_1$) satisfy subject reduction, compile to unification-free checkers ($\mathcal{A}_0, \mathcal{A}_1$), and match declarative typing. Third, we organize external verifiers into a three-level institutional hierarchy with explicit axiom policies (Adopt, Discharge, Relativize), internalize a justification logic with Why-provenance support $supp(j,P)$, and embed Cooper's Type Theory with Records (TTR) for open-world knowledge graphs. Finally, we prove consistency in Grothendieck universes and mechanize the metatheory in Lean 4 with zero sorry axioms.

papers.title: Probabilistic State Space Enumeration in Neural Network Computation
papers.abstract: Many methods for pruning neural networks rank weights or groups of weights by importance and retain a single subset. We study how channel groups contribute jointly to the output of multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) in Transformer language models. Inspired by network reliability analysis, probabilistic state space enumeration (PSSE) represents the dense MLP output as the expected importance-corrected masked output over $2^G$ joint states of $G$ channel groups. Summing the most probable states' probability-weighted outputs gives an approximation whose absolute error is bounded by the omitted probability mass times the maximum masked-output norm. NORDER-II adapts ORDER-II to enumerate states in decreasing probability without sorting the full space. Its first $B$ states maximize the probability mass captured at that budget. A weight-entropy scorer fixes each layer's ordering from pretrained weights. We evaluate all 168 MLP layers across six models from the Llama, Gemma, and Qwen families on two datasets with 8, 16, and 32 channel groups. In all 1,008 comparisons, the 95%-mass prefix yields lower mean relative error than uniform sampling at the same state count, with or without bias correction. At all three group counts, it also yields lower median and 99th-percentile relative error than a single top-$k$ mask. For downstream inference, we use the number of distinct channels in each prefix to set pruned MLP widths. With one validation-selected group count per model, PSSE achieves lower perplexity than both top-$k$ pruning baselines in all 36 matched-FLOP settings. Our pruned decoder MLPs achieve mean speedups of $1.11\times$, $1.23\times$, and $1.36\times$ over dense MLPs at 10%, 20%, and 30% target MLP projection FLOP savings, respectively. PSSE offers a principled path toward both probability-mass-controlled approximation and more efficient inference in pretrained language models.

papers.title: obfsgen: Generative Tunnel Obfuscation
papers.abstract: Encrypted tunnels are widely used to circumvent censorship, which has drawn censors' efforts to detect and block them. As the circumvention tunnels in widest use have largely converged on TLS, detection has shifted from the content of their traffic to its shape, where recent research and real-world blocking events have revealed exploitable fingerprints of tunneling. Existing traffic-shaping obfuscators such as obfs4, however, are fundamentally limited in hiding these fingerprints, as their application-driven design can only add to the shape that the application creates. A schedule-driven obfuscator, which decides when and how much to send independently of the application, can give tunnels any shape but raises new challenges, first and foremost what a good shape is. This paper presents obfsgen, a schedule-driven obfuscator for tunneling traffic. obfsgen samples its schedule from a generative sequence model of normal traffic, which predicts the future shape of a flow from its whole history, to capture the long-range dependencies that make a flow's shape normal. Built around this model, obfsgen addresses system problems that such an obfuscator faces in practice, such as synchronization across a noisy network. We evaluate the (in)distinguishability that obfsgen offers, the performance overhead that it adds and the computational resources that it requires. We see the schedule-driven architecture as the next generation of tunnel obfuscators, and we hope that obfsgen and the rationale behind its design help make such obfuscators practical and deployable.

papers.title: Complete Intersection Semigroups and End Curves on Singularities of Splice Type
papers.abstract: We prove that any complete intersection numerical semigroup can be realized as the value semigroup of an end curve in a splice quotient singularity. Therefore, providing a converse to the semigroup-theoretic statement of the End Curve Theorem of Neumann and Wahl for integral homology sphere links. For a certain family of curves embedded on splice quotient singularities with $\mathbb{Z}HS^3$ link, we show the coincidence between the Alexander polynomial of the knot cutted out by the curve and its Poincar\'e series. Hence providing a generalization of the result due to Campillo, Delgado and Gusein-Zade for plane curve singularities. Moreover, for any complete-intersection numerical semigroup, we define a family of knots such that the Alexander polynomial of the knots coincides with the generating series of the semigroup.

papers.title: GenPFN: An In-Context Tabular Foundation Model Approach for Augmenting Small Datasets in Engineering
papers.abstract: Costly simulations and experiments limit the data available for engineering design. This paper proposes GenPFN, a training-free candidate generator guided by a pretrained tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN) classifier with fixed weights. The context contains evaluated designs labeled desired (Class 1) or undesired (Class 0). GenPFN interpolates between desired designs and refines candidates using gated classifier gradients and Gaussian noise. Each candidate is evaluated using the problem's constraints and objective functions. Evaluated desired designs and their objective values augment the context for regression training. Evaluation spans fourteen selected problems, including a two-parameter benchmark and a 44-parameter hull problem. In paired comparisons, GenPFN with TabPFN v1 achieves higher class satisfaction and lower realism distance than the tested adversarial, variational-autoencoder and diffusion generators. The variational-autoencoder generator provides greater coverage and diversity. Relative to the synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE), GenPFN provides lower coverage distance and greater diversity. Among observed paired regression fits, augmentation reduces estimated AutoGluon validation mean squared error by 62.1% relative to context-only training. A hull-stern case study yields 99.3% propeller-compatible candidates versus 1.4% among randomly sampled context designs. Generation followed by evaluation produces sample sets that augment limited datasets and support training more accurate predictive models.

papers.title: A Characterization of Completely Integrally Closed Pr\"{u}fer $v$-Multiplication Domains
papers.abstract: We generalize a result known for Pr\"ufer domains to show that a PVMD $R$ is completely integrally closed if and only if $\text{Inv}^t(R)$ is an archimedean $\ell$-group. It has been conjectured that a PVMD is completely integrally closed if and only if it is an Archimedean domain. It is known that a completely integrally closed PVMD is an Archimedean domain. We provide an example to illustrate that an Archimedean PVMD need not be completely integrally closed.

papers.title: Random Sequential Adsorption versus the Uniform Ensemble of Jammed Configurations: Stochastic Dominance on Graphs
papers.abstract: Random sequential adsorption with nearest-neighbor exclusion on a graph, also known as the discrete parking process, ends in a jammed configuration, that is, a maximal independent set of the graph. We compare the number of occupied sites in two models: the sequential model generated by this dynamics, and the static model, in which all jammed configurations are equiprobable. In a recent study of the one-dimensional case, it was stated that the sequential occupancy first-order stochastically dominates the static one on every path graph; the proof was subsequently withdrawn and the statement left as a conjecture. We prove this conjecture for all path graphs. The dominance extends to all cycle graphs, and exact computations confirm it for all 31 connected graphs with fewer than 6 vertices. It is not universal: we construct graphs with 6 or more vertices and maximum degree at least 4 on which the static model dominates the sequential one, and although the two models are comparable on all connected graphs with up to 7 vertices, stochastic comparability fails starting at 8 vertices. We also prove that dominance is inherited by disjoint unions whose components share the same dominance direction, and we exhibit mixed unions in which comparability is either preserved or lost. Finally, supported by exhaustive computations, we conjecture that the sequential model dominates the static one on every graph with maximum degree at most 3, a class that includes paths, cycles, and ladder graphs.

papers.title: Strongly supercooled first-order phase transitions: monopole abundance, entropy production and homogeneity consistency
papers.abstract: We investigate whether monopole production in the early universe from a first-order phase transition in a unified gauge theory can be significantly suppressed if the phase transition is subject to strong supercooling but still completes successfully. This is facilitated by adopting a Gaussian nucleation model and assuming the false vacuum energy released is transferred to sectors which behave effectively as radiation in terms of cosmological evolution. We distinguish three criteria of phase-transition completion: the comoving measure completion (CMC) characterized by the eventual vanishing of the false-vacuum fraction (FVF), the physical volume completion (PVC) characterized by the eventual vanishing of the physical volume of false vacuum, and the asymptotic thermodynamic completion (ATC), which refers to the finiteness of total entropy production. Assuming an idealized Friedmann-Lema\^itre-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) cosmology, it is shown that the three criteria share exactly the same completion boundary, away from which they are completely equivalent. It is further shown that monopole abundance can be arbitrarily suppressed for parameter points approaching the completion boundary from the successful side. Nevertheless, for parameter points too close to the completion boundary, justification of the self-consistency of a homogeneous FLRW cosmology is difficult. We propose the use of the Hubble-scale FVF root-mean-square fluctuation to diagnose the homogeneity consistency issue, and find that arbitrarily strong suppression of monopole abundance relative to a reasonable Kibble estimate is not justifiable in terms of homogeneity consistency. These findings also have implications for gravitational wave production in strongly supercooled phase transitions.

papers.title: Invariance can prevent overfitting and shortcut learning in Quantum Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Many image classification tasks have labels that are unchanged by rotations and reflections. Equivariant quantum neural networks incorporate such symmetries by design, but the specific benefit of symmetry is difficult to isolate. Equivariant quantum circuits are usually compared with architectures that also differ in gates, structure or size. Here, we investigate the role of invariance in a controlled setting, classifying images whose labels are invariant under the dihedral group $D_4$. We compare four eight-qubit models with identical encoding, circuit structure and number of trainable parameters, and equivalent dynamical Lie algebras, and benchmark invariant implementations against non-invariant ones in terms of generalization error, robustness to shortcut learning and resilience to a realistic noise model. On four binary tasks, including MNIST and two scientific data sets of galaxies and red blood cells, the invariant models trained on a few tens of images show better generalization than non-invariant ones. Invariance also makes the models immune to orientation shortcuts: when trained with a class-dependent corner watermark, the non-invariant models learn the watermark and often drop to chance level when it is moved. We show that the gain in accuracy of invariant models persists also under a realistic noise model.

papers.title: Where can Gauss--Bonnet scalarization begin in neutron and quark stars, and when do stars carry scalar charge?
papers.abstract: In scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, with a coupling $\zeta(\phi)\mathcal G$, the Gauss-Bonnet invariant $\mathcal G$ sources the scalar when $\zeta'(0)\neq0$ and sets the sign of the effective mass squared of its perturbations when $\zeta$ is quadratic, so the surface on which $\mathcal G$ changes sign inside a star organises both the scalar flux and the regions in which spontaneous scalarization can begin. A regular static star with continuous density contains a surface $\Sigma$ on which $\mathcal G$ vanishes whenever its surface density is below half its mean density, and $\Sigma$ is unique when the density profile steepens outward and $p/\rho$ decreases. Neutron-star models without density discontinuities therefore have one, but self-bound stars need not: in the MIT bag model $\mathcal G<0$ inside every stable quark star, for any bag constant. For a quadratic coupling the tachyonic region is then, in a quark star, either the whole interior or the whole exterior, according to the sign of $\zeta''(0)$, whereas in a neutron star it includes part of the interior for either sign. In the Newtonian limit $\Sigma$ lies where $\rho=\bar\rho/2$ in every dimension. Over a whole slice the lapse-weighted integral of $\mathcal G$ equals the lapse-weighted Gauss-Bonnet curvature of space, which vanishes identically in three dimensions, so regular stars carry no scalar charge when $D=4$. Above four dimensions every star, isotropic or anisotropic, carries a scalar monopole given by an interior integral weighted by $\rho+p_r$. Under the radial null energy condition its sign is that of $\zeta'(0)$ for any equation of state, opposite to that of a Schwarzschild-Tangherlini black hole at the same order, and its size relative to the exterior contribution is of first post-Newtonian order.

papers.title: A resolution of the Erd\H{o}s similarity problem in the large
papers.abstract: We show that for every unbounded set $A\subset\mathbb R$ and every $0<\varepsilon<1$, there exists a closed set $S\subset\mathbb R$ that has measure at least $1-\varepsilon$ in every unit interval and contains no nontrivial affine copy of $A$. Moreover, $S$ can be chosen so that $|S\cap[x,x+1]|\to1$ as $|x|\to\infty$. This resolves the Erd\H{o}s similarity problem in the large.

papers.title: Triviality of metric fibrations over locally finite metric graphs
papers.abstract: In this note, we give a direct proof that every metric fibration over a geodesic metric space locally modeled on finite metric stars is isometrically isomorphic, over its base, to the $\ell^1$ product of its base and a fiber. Neither compactness nor completeness of the base is assumed. We also construct a nontrivial example over a closed interval with a truncated metric, showing that the local star condition alone does not imply the conclusion.

papers.title: NIF-VIO: Visual--Inertial Odometry Across Inertial and Non-Inertial Reference Frames
papers.abstract: Conventional visual--inertial odometry (VIO) assumes that observations from cameras and an inertial measurement unit (IMU) are jointly consistent in an inertial reference frame. However, this assumption breaks down under non-inertial conditions. Inside accelerating or rotating carriers, visual observations of the interior reflect carrier-relative motion, while IMU measurements contain additional carrier-induced components, which can compromise conventional fusion. We therefore present NIF-VIO for localization relative to the local environment across inertial and non-inertial reference frames. It adapts visual--inertial fusion based on measurement consistency. As inertial conditions change, early constraint isolation is combined with local reoptimization to limit error propagation before inconsistency confirmation and repair the affected local geometry. Under non-inertial conditions, a compact model with temporally shared parameters is introduced to account for carrier motion while preserving inertial information that complements visual constraints. Experiments on public benchmarks and a self-collected dataset demonstrate that NIF-VIO achieves competitive performance under inertial conditions and improved localization accuracy and availability under non-inertial conditions.

papers.title: How anion composition governs structural frameworks and Li-ion transport in oxychloride solid-state electrolytes
papers.abstract: Mixed-anion lithium oxychlorides exhibit high Li conductivity, but the relationship between oxygen content, structural framework, and Li-ion transport remains unclear. Here, crystal structure prediction and molecular dynamics simulations with machine-learning interatomic potentials are used to examine $\mathrm{Li}_yM\mathrm{O}_x\mathrm{Cl}_{6-2x}$ ($M$ = Nb and Ta [Group 5] and $M$ = Ti, Zr, and Hf [Group 4]). Increasing oxygen content changes isolated chloride-rich polyhedra into one-dimensional chains and subsequently more highly connected two- and three-dimensional frameworks. In the Group 5 series, fast Li diffusion occurs over $x \approx 0.67$--1.5, where the Li sites form a three-dimensional percolating network. Potential of mean force maps and nudged elastic band calculations reveal that fast Li-ion transport requires a low-dimensional framework supporting long-range migration through undercoordinated Li sites with low barriers, together with similar energies across Li sites. Finally, we perform fine-grid compositional search, which identifies $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{0.67}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.67}$, $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{0.75}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.5}$, $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$, and $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$ as stable candidates with predicted room-temperature self-diffusivities of up to $\sim 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{cm}^2/\mathrm{s}$. These findings establish how oxygen content controls framework and Li-ion transport, guiding the design of lithium oxyhalide electrolytes.

papers.title: A Perspective on Topological Charge Density Wave Materials
papers.abstract: Charge density waves are among the earliest known ordered states in quantum materials, yet they have re-emerged at the center of modern discussions of topology, symmetry breaking, and collective dynamics. In several material classes, charge-density-wave order reshapes electronic bands, boundary states, defect structures, and electromagnetic responses in ways that invite a topological interpretation. Real-space imaging has shown that incommensurate order can form networks of phase defects rather than uniform modulations. Boundary-resolved spectroscopy has revealed in-gap modes whose existence and spatial structure track the charge-density-wave order, although such observations remain confined to a single material family. In Weyl materials, density-wave gaps have been linked to axion-like magnetoelectric response, placing the charge-density-wave phase within a dynamical-field description of the effective action. In kagome metals, charge order is intertwined with Berry curvature, unconventional symmetry breaking, and superconductivity. These developments have led to the term "topological charge density wave," but the phrase describes several physically distinct phenomena. We distinguish three meanings: (i) topology of the order parameter and its defects, (ii) topology of the charge-density-wave-reconstructed electronic structure and its boundary modes, and (iii) axion-like electromagnetic response generated by density-wave order. The experimental and theoretical support for these three meanings differs substantially. This Perspective traces the development of these ideas, clarifies the evidence behind each class, identifies unresolved questions and points of debate, and outlines experimental criteria for establishing topology in charge-density-wave states.

papers.title: Measuring and Attributing Evidence Sensitivity in Medical Vision-Language Models via Symmetric Counterfactual Controls
papers.abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) asked closed clinical questions ("Is there a polyp?") can score well by relying on the question rather than the image, and current hallucination benchmarks cannot separate true visual discrimination from editing shortcuts or shifts in the answer threshold. We introduce a Counterfactual Evidence Framework that pairs each lesion erasure with a shape- and tool-matched control edit elsewhere in the image, adds same-site ring controls, restored and partial erasures, degraded views and natural negatives, tests on held-out inpainting tools, separates discrimination (the Evidence Sensitivity Gap, ESG, and AUROC) from the answer threshold, and checks the labels with blinded physician readers and hidden-state probes. Across 507 main-test cases (1,115 views), nine frontier VLMs claim 41.1% to 61.6% of erased lesions (ESG 0.269 to 0.470), whereas MedScope-4B, a Qwen3.5-4B agent trained on automatically built counterfactual trajectories, claims 9.6% (ESG 0.758; p <= 0.001 in all 27 primary comparisons). Physician readers support automated erasure in colonoscopy, where frontier models still claim 45% of erased lesions against 1% for MedScope-4B, but call a finding present on 54.7% of pooled erased reads across all sources, which bounds what unverified erasure can certify. Across 12 pre-registered training or system arms and 270 decision policies screened under a rule fixed in advance, every apparent utility gain comes from shifting the threshold rather than improving held-out discrimination, and probes point to perception as the remaining limit. We also report a 0/48 pneumothorax failure on an external cohort; retraining with pneumothorax patients in every stage finds 53% of pneumothoraxes on new patients without changing the main-test results.

papers.title: Exploration via Exploitation: The Blessing of Reward Diversity in Personalized Federated RL
papers.abstract: While federated reinforcement learning (RL) has traditionally guaranteed high efficiency in homogeneous environments, collaboration is often hindered when agents possess distinct goals. In this paper, we flip this paradigm, framing reward heterogeneity not as a hurdle to consensus, but as a structural asset that catalyzes exploration. We first propose Personalized Federated Upper Confidence Bound Value Iteration (PF-UCBVI), which achieves optimal linear speedup by decoupling shared dynamics from personalized objectives. To eliminate the risks of explicit exploration, we then introduce Personalized Federated Exploration-Free Value Iteration (PF-EFVI), a purely greedy algorithm that leverages reward diversity to ensure state-action coverage. We prove that PF-EFVI attains logarithmic regret without explicit exploration bonuses under sufficient reward diversity. Our results reveal that agent disagreement shifts the exploration burden from temporal complexity to spatial diversity, enabling efficient collective learning without explicit exploration.

papers.title: 2D Gum-Net: Unsupervised Dense Elastic Image Registration via Symmetric Correlation and Spectral Pooling
papers.abstract: Dense non-rigid registration, the recovery of a pixel-wise deformation field that warps one image into geometric agreement with another, is fundamental across medical imaging, structural biology, and correspondence estimation, yet learning-based approaches face a severe bottleneck: ground-truth deformation fields are notoriously difficult to obtain for real data. We present 2D Gum-Net, an end-to-end architecture that predicts dense elastic deformation fields fully unsupervised. We transfer the Geometric Unsupervised Matching Network (Gum-Net), originally developed for 3D subtomogram alignment in cryo-electron tomography, to 2D elastic registration: all three modules are redesigned in 2D, and the rigid transformation head is replaced by a Dense Spatial Transformer that regresses a sparse control-point grid, lifted to a full-resolution field $\Phi$ by bicubic interpolation. Downsampling uses DCT spectral pooling, implemented as frozen-basis matrix multiplications ($\approx 50\times$ GPU speedup), preserving the fine, quasi-periodic structure that max and average pooling destroy. We evaluate on contact-based fingerprints, a challenging testbed for this task: locally self-similar ridge patterns make correspondence maximally ambiguous, skin pressed against a sensor generates authentic large-displacement elastic distortion, and minutiae act as precise landmarks through which an independent matcher externally verifies the topological correctness of predicted fields. Trained purely on synthetic impressions and evaluated zero-shot on real benchmarks, our method improves structural correlation by up to 15.7% on FVC2004 and raises genuine match scores under an independent matcher while leaving imposter scores essentially unchanged. This suggests that the predicted deformations restore true structure without fabricating correspondences.
